articles.title: NOW Sports Membership Q&A: How do I stream Sky Sports? Is it instant? Is there a contract?
articles.summary: The below content is an advert
articles.body:
Want to stream Sky Sports with NOW? Great, go HERE!

What is NOW?

NOW is an instant streaming service offering access to all 12 Sky Sports channels, every Sky Sports+ stream, and much more.

It's an app, so customers can sign up and stream instantly across over 60 devices. It offers contract-free memberships options, so customers can cancel anytime!

You can choose between a Month or Day Memberships. The latest prices for each Membership option can be found here.

Sounds great! What channels do I get?

Memberships gives you access to:

  • Sky Sports Main Event
  • Sky Sports Premier League
  • Sky Sports Football
  • Sky Sports F1
  • Sky Sports Tennis
  • Sky Sports Cricket
  • Sky Sports Golf
  • Sky Sports+
  • Sky Sports Action
  • Sky Sports Racing
  • Sky Sports News
  • Sky Sports Mix

NOW Sports Memberships also give customers access to all live Sky Sports+ streams as well as Sky Sports documentaries and selected replays and highlights on demand within your Membership period.

N.B. Customers cannot access Sky Sports Box Office events via NOW.

So, I don't need a smart TV, stick or set-top box to get NOW?

No - you don't need one. You can watch NOW on over 60 different devices, including selected smart TVs and sticks, but also on smartphones, PC or Mac, plus PS4/PS5™, Xbox One & Xbox Series X/S consoles.

Watch online at NOWTV.com or download the app to watch on your smartphone, smart TV or games console.

See our full list of compatible devices.

If I sign up to NOW on one device, can I watch it on another?

Yes - you can sign up on one device and watch on another device of your choice. This sign-in journey varies by platform, but on Smart TVs for instance, you will be given a QR code function to sign in quickly.

However, customers without Boost cannot watch NOW on two devices at the same time.

The match I want to watch starts in 10 minutes, is the Membership instant?

Yes!

Can I watch without a contract?

Yes, NOW offers contract-free Sports Month & Day Memberships options, so customers can sign up and cancel anytime.

For your fully flexible Sports Month Membership, you'll still be able to stream until the end of that 30-day viewing period. If you don't cancel, it renews automatically at the end of the 30-day period.

What sports can I watch?

  • Premier League.
  • Carabao Cup.
  • EFL.
  • WSL.
  • Formula 1.
  • England Cricket home matches.
  • ICC Cricket Tournaments (e.g., Cricket World Cup)
  • All Golf Majors & Ryder Cup.
  • US Open, ATP & WTA Tour Tennis.
  • Premier League Darts.
  • Betfred Super League.
  • NFL.

How many devices can I watch on at the same time?

You can watch on one device as standard, up to two devices at the same time with NOW Boost, or up to three devices at the same time with NOW Ultra Boost.

What are NOW Boost and NOW Ultra Boost?

Upgrading to Boost means you can watch in Full HD, enjoy Dolby Digital 5.1 with your sound system or soundbar, get an extra device to stream on, and watch on-demand content ad-free.

Upgrading to Ultra Boost means you can watch in up to 4k UHD HDR, enjoy Dolby Atmos with your sound system or soundbar, get two extra devices to stream on, and watch on-demand content ad-free. Check device compatibility here.

To add Boost or Ultra Boost to your Sports Membership, head over to My Account section of the NOW website.

articles.summary: BBC Sport brings you the latest news, punditry, analysis, fan views, stats and gossip on your favourite club.
articles.body:
We have got your team covered with bespoke pages for Premier League, Championship and Scottish Premiership clubs.

There is also a page rounding up all the key news and insight from the Women's Super League.

It is your one-stop shop for the latest news, insight, expert analysis, fan views, stats and gossip.

To get started, choose your club from the list below.

Once there, hit 'Follow' to make sure you do not miss a beat.

If you are on the BBC Sport app, you can use the bell icon to sign up for news alerts - and if signed in on a browser, you will start seeing more content about your club on your BBC Sport homepage.

Have you got a question about your Premier League club? Get in touch here and we'll seek answers

You can also get the latest stories on every club in League One, League Two and the National League in England, and the Championship, League One and League Two in Scotland.

It's the same process as above - choose your club from the list below, and once there, hit 'Follow'.

articles.title: Sky Sports push notifications FAQ: How to receive the news alerts you want
articles.summary: The Sky Sports mobile app will keep you up to date with the latest news from your favourite sports - here's how to receive the alerts you want.
articles.body:
The Sky Sports mobile app will keep you up to date with the latest news from your favourite sports - here's how to receive the alerts you want.

Choose from streaming the live action on your mobile or tablet, receiving breaking news straight to your device or being notified when highlights from your favourite sports are available to watch so you don't miss a moment while out and about.

And this season, you can also watch vertical clips of the best Premier League action in the Sky Sports app!

Here's how....

For the best app and vertical video experience, make sure you have the latest version downloaded onto your phone or tablet.

Once you have updated to the latest version of the app and signed in, you can enjoy all the latest available features for the new Premier League season including vertical video highlights and filter Sky Sports' notifications to suit your needs...

Q: I want to be notified when a big sports news story breaks, but I don't want to sign up to receive individual sports alerts. Can I do that?

A: Yes! On the app home page, tap on the 'Profile' icon in the bottom-right hand corner and then tap notifications. On the next page, simply tap on 'Breaking News' and we'll send you a notification when a big story emerges. This way, you'll be notified when a top story arrives - but you won't receive daily individual sports alerts.

Q: I'm a football fan, but I'm keen to know when a big sports story breaks. I want to get all the latest football news, but would like to know who has won the latest Formula 1 Grand Prix or the result of a big Box Office event, for example. Is that possible?

A: It is! If you're keen on getting dedicated news alerts from an individual sport but want to know when a big sports story breaks, make sure you tap on the sport you love along with 'Breaking News'. This way, you'll be notified of a big story without having to subscribe to another sport.

Q: I want to receive the latest football, tennis, rugby league, darts, golf and boxing news. Can I subscribe to more than one sport?

A: Of course! Tap on the sports you love and we'll send you a notification when a story comes in. Click on as many sports as you'd like, and we'll keep you updated. You can choose from Football, F1, Cricket, Boxing, Golf, Tennis, Rugby League, Rugby Union, Darts, NFL, Boxing, Horse Racing and Netball.

Q: I want to be notified when there's a big event on Sky Sports coming up or about to start. Can I get notifications reminding me when coverage of a Grand Prix on Sky Sports F1 is under way, or who's playing on Super Sunday on Sky Sports Premier League?

A: Simply select 'Live on Sky' to receive alerts on the best live action on our dedicated channels.

Q: What if I change my mind and want to stop receiving alerts?

A: You can toggle sports, 'Breaking News' and 'Live on Sky' on and off as you see fit, then you'll only receive the alerts you want us to send you.

Remember, for the best app and vertical video experience, make sure you download the latest version onto your phone or tablet.

articles.title: Fans react to Cape Verde’s shocking draw against Spain in World Cup debut | CNN
articles.summary: The island nation of Cape Verde shocked fans in their first-ever World Cup match by earning a draw against reigning European champions, Spain. Fans in Atlanta, where the match was held, celebrated by cheering, dancing and even singing Shakira’s “Waka Waka (This Time for Africa),” which was the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup.
articles.body:
The island nation of Cape Verde shocked fans in their first-ever World Cup match by earning a draw against reigning European champions, Spain. Fans in Atlanta, where the match was held, celebrated by cheering, dancing and even singing Shakira's "Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)," which was the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

articles.title: Julian Nagelsmann resigns as Germany head coach after shock World Cup exit with Jurgen Klopp 'ready' to take over
articles.summary: Julian Nagelsmann leaves head coach role after Germany's World Cup exit; Nagelsmann had been in charge of Germany since September 2023; German FA confirms intention to now seek talks with former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp who has confirmed his interest in replacing Nagelsmann
articles.body:
Jurgen Klopp is set to hold talks with officials from the German FA in New York next week about becoming the national team boss, according to Sky in Germany.

The former Liverpool boss confirmed his interest in succeeding Julian Nagelsmann and that he had been approached about the role in an interview with Magenta TV on Friday.

"Yes, I can confirm the talks," he said. "Things moved along quite quickly. Julian has resigned and the DFB is working on a successor. And in the course of these considerations, they approached me."

  • Germany crash out of World Cup on penalties to Paraguay
  • Germany were once World Cup kings. Now they're simply not that good
  • World Cup day-by-day schedule | Latest: World Cup
  • Follow our World Cup coverage in the Sky Sports App

The German Football Association does not believe it will be an issue getting Klopp out of his current job as global head of football at Red Bull.

It would be the first time the German FA has paid a fee to appoint a coach, with Klopp having a contract with Red Bull until 2029 which includes a special exit clause for the Germany job.

Klopp said: "I have an existing contract with Red Bull. I've said many times how much I enjoy this job. As a person, I usually honour contracts. But I've also made it clear that I'm interested in talks with the DFB.

Klopp said he does not expect his current employers to stand in his way - and is ready to return to management in the capacity as a national team boss two years after his Liverpool exit.

"Now isn't the perfect timing. But it's better than it's ever been. I'm more than refuelled now, I'm ready," Klopp said.

Klopp eyeing up first managerial job in two years

Nagelsmann stepped down from the role after Germany's shock World Cup last-32 exit against Paraguay.

DFB president Bernd Neuendorf said ⁠in a statement on Friday: "The ⁠German Football Association expressly thanks Julian ‌Nagelsmann for his work since September 2023. ‌He is characterised by a high level of commitment and extraordinary ambition. ⁠Julian Nagelsmann is ​also an extremely ​responsible and sincere ​person whom we all ⁠value."

The statement added: "Regarding the appointment of a new coach, the DFB leadership will now seek talks with Jurgen Klopp. He has already signalled his general willingness to take on the position."

If Klopp makes the move it would be his first coaching job since leaving Liverpool in 2024.

Nagelsmann, 38, took charge of Germany in September 2023 and guided the nation to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were beaten by eventual winners Spain.

Germany were knocked out of the 2026 World Cup by Paraguay on penalties, following a 1-1 draw after extra-time in Boston. They had topped Group E on goal difference after thrashing newcomers Curacao 7-1 in their opening game and beating Ivory Coast 2-1, before a 2-1 defeat to Ecuador.

"I am not someone who runs away," Nagelsmann had said after the 2014 winners were dumped out.

"This is not the first time this has happened, and there are some things about today that need to be changed.

"But if the DFB wants me to continue I am going to continue. I know the mechanics of football, I know how the industry works.

"I know a lot of people will want me to leave but I would love to continue if the football association wants me to."

Klopp coaching Germany 'would be dream come true'

Sky Germany reporter Dennis Bayer:

"It would be a dream come true that many Germans had for a lot of years.

"For more-or-less a decade, people in Germany have been talking about how good it would be if Jurgen Klopp would become the national coach and now it seems like it is going to happen.

"The DFB itself confirmed that it will talk with Jurgen Klopp in the next days - and he has already given his initial go [ahead] and said that he could imagine being Germany next national coach.

"He's still in a job in Leipzig as head of global soccer (for the Red Bull group) and there are talks that have to be made.

"But there is a good chance that Jurgen Klopp returns to the sidelines and becomes the new head coach of Germany. That's something that many, many, many Germans have wanted for years."

It would be the first time the German FA has paid a fee to appoint a coach, with Klopp having a contract with Red Bull until 2029 which includes a special exit clause for the Germany job.

Klopp said: "I have an existing contract with Red Bull. I've said many times how much I enjoy this job. As a person, I usually honour contracts. But I've also made it clear that I'm interested in talks with the DFB.

Klopp said he does not expect his current employers to stand in his way - and is ready to return to management in the capacity as a national team boss two years after his Liverpool exit.

"Now isn't the perfect timing. But it's better than it's ever been. I'm more than refuelled now, I'm ready," Klopp said.

Klopp eyeing up first managerial job in two years

Nagelsmann stepped down from the role after Germany's shock World Cup last-32 exit against Paraguay.

DFB president Bernd Neuendorf said ⁠in a statement on Friday: "The ⁠German Football Association expressly thanks Julian ‌Nagelsmann for his work since September 2023. ‌He is characterised by a high level of commitment and extraordinary ambition. ⁠Julian Nagelsmann is ​also an extremely ​responsible and sincere ​person whom we all ⁠value."

The statement added: "Regarding the appointment of a new coach, the DFB leadership will now seek talks with Jurgen Klopp. He has already signalled his general willingness to take on the position."

If Klopp makes the move it would be his first coaching job since leaving Liverpool in 2024.

Nagelsmann, 38, took charge of Germany in September 2023 and guided the nation to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were beaten by eventual winners Spain.

Germany were knocked out of the 2026 World Cup by Paraguay on penalties, following a 1-1 draw after extra-time in Boston. They had topped Group E on goal difference after thrashing newcomers Curacao 7-1 in their opening game and beating Ivory Coast 2-1, before a 2-1 defeat to Ecuador.

"I am not someone who runs away," Nagelsmann had said after the 2014 winners were dumped out.

"This is not the first time this has happened, and there are some things about today that need to be changed.

"But if the DFB wants me to continue I am going to continue. I know the mechanics of football, I know how the industry works.

"I know a lot of people will want me to leave but I would love to continue if the football association wants me to."

Klopp coaching Germany 'would be dream come true'

Sky Germany reporter Dennis Bayer:

"It would be a dream come true that many Germans had for a lot of years.

"For more-or-less a decade, people in Germany have been talking about how good it would be if Jurgen Klopp would become the national coach and now it seems like it is going to happen.

"The DFB itself confirmed that it will talk with Jurgen Klopp in the next days - and he has already given his initial go [ahead] and said that he could imagine being Germany next national coach.

"He's still in a job in Leipzig as head of global soccer (for the Red Bull group) and there are talks that have to be made.

"But there is a good chance that Jurgen Klopp returns to the sidelines and becomes the new head coach of Germany. That's something that many, many, many Germans have wanted for years."

articles.title: Carabao Cup 2026-27: When is the third-round draw and which teams are in it?
articles.summary: The third-round draw of the EFL Cup takes place on Wednesday, with nine Premier League teams entering the competition at this stage.
articles.body:
The third-round draw for the 2026-27 Carabao Cup will take place on Wednesday, 26 August following the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nine Premier League clubs taking part in European football join the 23 first-round winners from across the English Football League.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Sunderland, Brighton and Crystal Palace will enter the competition at this stage, as the top eight Premier League clubs from the 2025-26 season plus Crystal Palace as Conference League winners.

It will be broadcast live on Sky Sports following the conclusion of the third round tie between Preston North End and Everton, kicking off at 20:00 BST that evening.

Unlike the opening two rounds of the competition, the third round draw is not regionalised.

However, before the match at Deepdale there will be a pre-draw determining which of the Champions League and Europa League clubs will play at home or away in round three.

In order to avoid potential scheduling issues, the eight Champions League and Europa League clubs cannot be drawn against each other in round three.

When the draw takes place, the first eight fixtures decided are the ones involving clubs in the Champions League and Europa League. The remainder of the draw will be an open draw as usual.

Due to clashes with opening weeks of the Champions League and Europa League seasons, the third round will be played across two different weeks. They are the weeks commencing Monday, 7 and Monday, 14 September, 2026.

articles.title: Lionel Messi: The Argentine's most iconic moments as he ponders retirement
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi considers his footballing future following the death of his father, BBC Sport looks back at some of his most iconic moments.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi is considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge.

The 39-year-old Argentina forward is signed with Inter Miami until 2028.

But, in an emotional tribute to his dad, he hinted at retirement as he said: "I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer."

He has scored a combined 921 goals for Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Inter Miami and Argentina.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of his remarkable career.

Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death Published 12 August

Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death

A rivalry that changed football Published 5 June

'That's why he's the king' - Messi sets up third World Cup final Published 16 July

'That's why he's the king' - Messi sets up third World Cup final

First hat-trick as teenager shows talent

Messi's first career hat-trick came in one of the biggest fixtures in football - El Clasico.

At the age of 19, he scored all of Barcelona's goals in a 3-3 draw against rivals Real Madrid on 10 March 2007 - his first at the Camp Nou - including a brilliant last-minute finish after beating a couple of defenders.

This was arguably the moment he became a household name.

Sublime solo strike sparks Maradona memories

Just over a month after that hat-trick, Messi scored a goal he has probably never surpassed in the rest of his glorious career.

It came in a 5-2 win over Getafe in the Copa del Rey semi-final first leg on 18 April 2007.

In a strike with remarkable similarities to compatriot Diego Maradona's (non-handball) effort against England in the 1986 World Cup, Messi picked the ball up in his own half, beat about five defenders, went around the goalkeeper and slotted home.

Ridiculous as it sounds now, back in 2009 some English football fans and journalists questioned whether Messi could do it against English opponents in Europe - having failed to net in 10 Champions League appearances against Premier League sides.

But there were no more doubts when Messi rose highest in the box to head home Xavi's cross in his first Champions League final against Manchester United - and the first game billed as Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo.

Two years later he would score in another final win over Sir Alex Ferguson's men to claim the third of his four Champions League winners' medals.

Messi scored four goals for the first time in his career as he took Arsenal to the cleaners in the 2010 Champions League quarter-final for a 4-1 home-leg win.

The pick of the bunch was his chip over keeper Manuel Almunia to complete his hat-trick.

An honourable mention goes to his five-goal haul two years later against Bayer Leverkusen in a 7-1 last-16 success.

He is the second top scorer in Champions League history with 129, behind Ronaldo.

Messi broke Barcelona's goalscoring record - aged just 24 - in some style with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Granada on 20 March 2012.

He equalled Cesar Rodriguez's 60-year-old record of 232 goals with his first, broke it with his second and extended the record with a third.

By the time he left Barcelona in 2021 he had extended that mark to 672 goals.

A stat so amazing you have to go back to double check to make sure it really happened.

In 2012 Messi hit his 91st goal of the year in Barcelona's 3-1 win at Real Valladolid on 22 December.

It earned him a place in the Guinness Book of Records. , external

He netted 79 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina - in a total of 69 games for club and country.

It was enough to earn Messi a then-unprecedented fourth consecutive Ballon d'Or - even though he only won the Copa del Rey in 2012 for all those goals.

This was the second major record Messi broke with a hat-trick.

He hit three in a 5-1 win over Sevilla on 22 November 2014 to become the top scorer in La Liga's history.

Messi equalled Telmo Zarra's 251-goal mark - set in 1955 by the Athletic Club forward - with a free-kick, before breaking it and stretching it with a third.

He ended up on 474 goals, far clear of Ronaldo's 311 for Real Madrid.

A 500th Barcelona goal - and in another El Clasico

All the narratives seemed to come together in Barcelona's 3-2 win at Real Madrid on 23 April 2017.

Messi popped up with an injury-time goal, sweeping home a first-time shot from the edge of the area. It was an El Clasico winner, his 500th Barcelona goal and it sent his side top of the table - although Real would go on to win the league at the end of that season.

For good measure, he pulled out an iconic celebration when he took off his shirt and held it out so the Bernabeu faithful could see his name.

The almost unthinkable happened in August 2021 as Messi left Barcelona on a free transfer.

After 21 years, 672 goals and 35 trophies, he had to leave because the club could not afford to honour the new contract they agreed because of La Liga's salary limit.

In an emotional news conference, a tearful Messi said: "My family and I were convinced we were going to stay here, at home.

"I don't want to leave this club - it's a club I love and this is a moment I didn't expect."

Despite being linked with Manchester City, he joined Paris St-Germain.

First international trophy with Argentina

On 11 July, 2021, Messi - at the age of 34 - won his first senior international trophy as Argentina beat Brazil 1-0 in the Copa America final at the Maracana.

He was named player of the tournament after scoring four goals.

An emotional Messi fell to the ground as the full-time whistle blew and was thrown in the air by his team-mates as they celebrated.

He won his second Copa America three years later.

It was a triumph and moment that looked like it would never happen, with Messi having previously retired from international football before coming back.

It was always the thing held against him in debates about whether he was the greatest footballer of all time.

Messi scored two goals, and his effort in the 2022 shootout, as Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the best World Cup final ever.

He was named player of the tournament, having netted seven times - including efforts in each knockout round.

Messi won another two Ballons d'Or after leaving Barcelona - one at Paris St-Germain and one at Inter Miami - to extend his record haul to eight.

His last one came in October 2023 after he won the World Cup and helped his Major League Soccer side lift the Leagues Cup for their first trophy.

"I couldn't imagine having the career I've had and everything I've achieved, the fortune I've had to be part of the best team in history," he said.

"All of them [Ballon d'Or awards] are special for different reasons."

The World Cup's top scorer - albeit briefly

If 2026 was to be his last World Cup, Messi certainly went out in style.

His eight goals in the tournament took him 21 in the World Cup - more than anyone has ever scored, until Mbappe went past that tally to 22 in the Bronze Final defeat by England.

Aged 39, Messi's World Cup may have ended in disappointment - as Argentina lost to Spain in the final - but individually it was another month on football's biggest stage few will forget.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Draft Mistakes to Avoid: 6 things you  must eliminate from your game to have success
articles.summary: Sometimes the discussion needs to be about how to play, as opposed to who to pick. Scott Pianowski shares his draft mistakes to avoid.
articles.body:
For most of the summer, fantasy football managers have their scouting hats on. Who's running with the starters? What offenses look like fun? What players are likely to exceed expectations, or fall short of them?

But sometimes the discussion needs to be about how to play, as opposed to who to pick. And today we'll run through some of the draft mistakes I want you to eliminate from your game.

Mistake 1: Not being familiar with the rules

Just because it's obvious doesn't mean it can't be true. You gotta know the rules. It's a common error, and I know, because I make it myself sometimes — and there's no justification for it.

It's no fun to read the rules or audit the settings, I get it. In some of the leagues I play in, the rulebook is long and unwieldy, a cumbersome read. And like so many fantasy managers, I'm in a ton of leagues (too many to count), so at times it becomes tempting to cut this corner.

But if you're not clear on the game you're playing, errors are sure to follow. So let's make sure we put in the work. (Even if you don't want to audit the rules yourself, there are shortcuts — maybe one of the veterans of your league can give you the key points you need. Don't be afraid to ask.)

And with this overall tip, we're not just talking about checking scoring rules, but every league setting. Often managers are unaware of when free agency starts or when the waiver process begins, and miss out on key early-season acquisitions as a result. .

Thirty seconds in your online calendar today can cover you for a missed opportunity later.

Modern baseball theory says that sacrifice bunts are rarely a good idea. The game is dominated by launch angles and home runs, to the point that giving up an out and advancing a runner from first to second is rarely the proper play. When you hand outs to the other team, you cap your scoring upside.

What does this have to do with fantasy football? Well, when you go out of your way to draft the NFL backups of your primary starters (especially at running back), you're essentially bunting. You're capping your upside. You're playing for the small inning.

Early in the fantasy season, I want you to play for the big inning. I want you to try to build the most dynamic juggernaut possible. Sure, you can draft backup running backs, intriguing stash-and-hope runners, but do it when it's not tied to one of your primary starters.

Instead, target the backups that benefit if your opponents encounter bad luck.

We want to build a roster that can spike — not merely survive — when chaos happens. Stop playing it safe and hurting your ceiling.

I'm not dismissing RB insurance completely. The understudy back can make sense later in the year — much like bunting can still make sense in baseball, later in a game. The winning scenario narrows the later we get in any contest, and with that in mind, you act accordingly.

If you're crushing the league come early November and you want Brian Robinson Jr. to insure Bijan Robinson— because your roster doesn't have bigger problems that need solving — I can sign off.

In August, that's the wrong way to think. Your goals should be much loftier the day you start assembling your roster.

Mistake 3: Anchoring to previously-held opinions

Fantasy sports are essentially a game of opinions, your best guess against my best guess. The top fantasy managers are going to have plenty of takes. You compete for a few years, take down a trophy or two, you get some confidence and even some ego.

But remember the NFL is a snow-globe league, the American sport with the most year-over-year variance.

It's also the fantasy sport where context matters the most. Compare Saquon Barkley's final season with the Giants (a slog in 2023) versus his monster onboard with the Eagles (Offensive Player of the Year) in 2024.

I have plenty of strong player and strategy takes today, just like I did a month ago, three months ago or six months ago. But everything's written in pencil. When the facts shift, I'm certainly willing to change my mind. And when overlooked angles are brought to my attention, I'm willing to change my mind then, too.

We're aiming to figure out the new season before your opponents do. And with that in mind, let's be willing to be selectively aggressive when opportunities arise.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Paradox of Choice is a fascinating concept, the idea that otherwise-smart people can be overwhelmed by alternatives. It's not uncommon for a fantasy manager to tell me they prefer a roster of minimal depth over a roster of fantastic depth, because they aren't forced to make difficult choices each week. (Obviously, a deep team can allow for trades to build an even better starting lineup, but let's ignore that for now.)

Some managers are afraid to bench a player because said player was a high pick, or required a lot of FAB on the waiver wire.

Some managers are afraid to make a trade or a free agent move because they're obsessed with how bad they'll feel if the decision turns out to be wrong.

Friendliest Loss remains a pox in our decision-making world. Too many fantasy players will settle on the choice that will give them the least amount of pain if it doesn't go as planned — no matter if that choice reflects what they view the most likely winning scenario.

Don't be afraid of making a mistake, friends. Tricky decisions are like bluffs in poker — if you don't have one blow up on you every so often, you are playing far too conservatively. Fortune favors the brave.

I'm not suggesting you do wacky things just for the sake of it. I still want you to make good decisions, sound decisions. But focus on the likelihood of your decision working, and what the payoff may be. Don't get tripped up on what the regret will feel like if you're wrong. That's not how successful people think.

Mistake 5: Not updating your queue during the draft

I generally don't touch the preset rankings in any draft applet, because I want to know what most of the league is looking at. But that doesn't mean I rest back in my chair and scroll through emails between picks.

I'm constantly working on some kind of list, be it an off-applet list I'm maintaining, or adding and arranging players in my online draft queue.

A tidily-arranged queue will be your best friend if you get bumped offline mid-draft — and will spare you a possible-disastrous autopick. It's also a good way to keep late-round sleepers fresh in your mind, especially with names who might be buried on the site's preset ranks.

If you're doing an offline draft, you can still maintain a queue — a pen and sheet of paper will do. Just keep it away from curious neighbors.

Yahoo also offers a wealth of options to help managers during the draft with Yahoo Fantasy Plus and Ultra — learn more about tools and advice and consider subscribing .

College Fantasy Football 101: Learn how to play Yahoo's newest game

Bold College Fantasy Football predictions for the 2026 season

College Fantasy Football: 26 stats Eric Froton finds relevant as we approach the 2026 season

It's common to hear established fantasy players zealously proclaiming their disdain for average draft position , noting how they draft to the beat of their own drummer. And hey, I get it, at some point, you have to go get the players you believe in. But you at least want to have a general idea of where those players might come off the board in a typical draft.

When I examine ADP, I like to focus on the trending market, how rooms have been drafting in the past week or so — something you can track on Yahoo if you're a Plus or Ultra subscriber. Deeper-rooted ADP is going to be more buggy and less useful.

At the end of the day, you want to undercut the market slightly on the later-round picks you covet, not blow the market out of the water. Don't take your hidden gem in the sixth round when context clues make it clear you could have waited until the 10th round or later.

— Don't forget background checks : Do a quick view of the news a few hours before your draft, and if you have time while drafting, make use of the information tabs in the draft room. You don't want to be the last to know about someone's new hamstring injury.

Fantasy Football: 3 big-name quarterbacks we're fading at ADP this season

Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026

Fantasy Football Running Back Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the RB profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook

— Don't worry too much about bye weeks : If you want to break a tie between similar players based on their bye weeks and what fits your roster, I'm fine with it. But it's a lower priority. When in doubt, give me the later bye week — your roster will look a lot different in late October or November. But for the most part, I ignore the bye weeks. Just go get talent.

— Don't stop analyzing your neighborhood : The roster construction of teams around you will impact many of your choices. Often times I can break a tie between two different positions of need based on what my neighbors are most likely to do with their picks, based on their current shape.

— Don't lose sight of tier drops : Understanding where talent clusters and where talent drops off is critical to any successful draft. This is especially paramount in salary cap formats , where you desperately want to be landing your players while your opponents still have similar alternatives — so that panic buying doesn't set in.

And with this overall tip, we're not just talking about checking scoring rules, but every league setting. Often managers are unaware of when free agency starts or when the waiver process begins, and miss out on key early-season acquisitions as a result. .
Thirty seconds in your online calendar today can cover you for a missed opportunity later.

Modern baseball theory says that sacrifice bunts are rarely a good idea. The game is dominated by launch angles and home runs, to the point that giving up an out and advancing a runner from first to second is rarely the proper play. When you hand outs to the other team, you cap your scoring upside.

What does this have to do with fantasy football? Well, when you go out of your way to draft the NFL backups of your primary starters (especially at running back), you're essentially bunting. You're capping your upside. You're playing for the small inning.

Early in the fantasy season, I want you to play for the big inning. I want you to try to build the most dynamic juggernaut possible. Sure, you can draft backup running backs, intriguing stash-and-hope runners, but do it when it's not tied to one of your primary starters.
Instead, target the backups that benefit if your opponents encounter bad luck.
We want to build a roster that can spike — not merely survive — when chaos happens. Stop playing it safe and hurting your ceiling.

I'm not dismissing RB insurance completely. The understudy back can make sense later in the year — much like bunting can still make sense in baseball, later in a game. The winning scenario narrows the later we get in any contest, and with that in mind, you act accordingly.
If you're crushing the league come early November and you want Brian Robinson Jr. to insure Bijan Robinson— because your roster doesn't have bigger problems that need solving — I can sign off.
In August, that's the wrong way to think. Your goals should be much loftier the day you start assembling your roster.
Mistake 3: Anchoring to previously-held opinions

Fantasy sports are essentially a game of opinions, your best guess against my best guess. The top fantasy managers are going to have plenty of takes. You compete for a few years, take down a trophy or two, you get some confidence and even some ego.
But remember the NFL is a snow-globe league, the American sport with the most year-over-year variance.

It's also the fantasy sport where context matters the most. Compare Saquon Barkley's final season with the Giants (a slog in 2023) versus his monster onboard with the Eagles (Offensive Player of the Year) in 2024.

I have plenty of strong player and strategy takes today, just like I did a month ago, three months ago or six months ago. But everything's written in pencil. When the facts shift, I'm certainly willing to change my mind. And when overlooked angles are brought to my attention, I'm willing to change my mind then, too.
We're aiming to figure out the new season before your opponents do. And with that in mind, let's be willing to be selectively aggressive when opportunities arise.
Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Paradox of Choice is a fascinating concept, the idea that otherwise-smart people can be overwhelmed by alternatives. It's not uncommon for a fantasy manager to tell me they prefer a roster of minimal depth over a roster of fantastic depth, because they aren't forced to make difficult choices each week. (Obviously, a deep team can allow for trades to build an even better starting lineup, but let's ignore that for now.)
Some managers are afraid to bench a player because said player was a high pick, or required a lot of FAB on the waiver wire.
Some managers are afraid to make a trade or a free agent move because they're obsessed with how bad they'll feel if the decision turns out to be wrong.

Friendliest Loss remains a pox in our decision-making world. Too many fantasy players will settle on the choice that will give them the least amount of pain if it doesn't go as planned — no matter if that choice reflects what they view the most likely winning scenario.

Don't be afraid of making a mistake, friends. Tricky decisions are like bluffs in poker — if you don't have one blow up on you every so often, you are playing far too conservatively. Fortune favors the brave.

I'm not suggesting you do wacky things just for the sake of it. I still want you to make good decisions, sound decisions. But focus on the likelihood of your decision working, and what the payoff may be. Don't get tripped up on what the regret will feel like if you're wrong. That's not how successful people think.
Mistake 5: Not updating your queue during the draft

I generally don't touch the preset rankings in any draft applet, because I want to know what most of the league is looking at. But that doesn't mean I rest back in my chair and scroll through emails between picks.
I'm constantly working on some kind of list, be it an off-applet list I'm maintaining, or adding and arranging players in my online draft queue.

A tidily-arranged queue will be your best friend if you get bumped offline mid-draft — and will spare you a possible-disastrous autopick. It's also a good way to keep late-round sleepers fresh in your mind, especially with names who might be buried on the site's preset ranks.
If you're doing an offline draft, you can still maintain a queue — a pen and sheet of paper will do. Just keep it away from curious neighbors.
Yahoo also offers a wealth of options to help managers during the draft with Yahoo Fantasy Plus and Ultra — learn more about tools and advice and consider subscribing .
College Fantasy Football 101: Learn how to play Yahoo's newest game
Bold College Fantasy Football predictions for the 2026 season
College Fantasy Football: 26 stats Eric Froton finds relevant as we approach the 2026 season

It's common to hear established fantasy players zealously proclaiming their disdain for average draft position , noting how they draft to the beat of their own drummer. And hey, I get it, at some point, you have to go get the players you believe in. But you at least want to have a general idea of where those players might come off the board in a typical draft.

When I examine ADP, I like to focus on the trending market, how rooms have been drafting in the past week or so — something you can track on Yahoo if you're a Plus or Ultra subscriber. Deeper-rooted ADP is going to be more buggy and less useful.

At the end of the day, you want to undercut the market slightly on the later-round picks you covet, not blow the market out of the water. Don't take your hidden gem in the sixth round when context clues make it clear you could have waited until the 10th round or later.

— Don't forget background checks : Do a quick view of the news a few hours before your draft, and if you have time while drafting, make use of the information tabs in the draft room. You don't want to be the last to know about someone's new hamstring injury.
Fantasy Football: 3 big-name quarterbacks we're fading at ADP this season
Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026
Fantasy Football Running Back Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the RB profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook

— Don't worry too much about bye weeks : If you want to break a tie between similar players based on their bye weeks and what fits your roster, I'm fine with it. But it's a lower priority. When in doubt, give me the later bye week — your roster will look a lot different in late October or November. But for the most part, I ignore the bye weeks. Just go get talent.

— Don't stop analyzing your neighborhood : The roster construction of teams around you will impact many of your choices. Often times I can break a tie between two different positions of need based on what my neighbors are most likely to do with their picks, based on their current shape.

— Don't lose sight of tier drops : Understanding where talent clusters and where talent drops off is critical to any successful draft. This is especially paramount in salary cap formats , where you desperately want to be landing your players while your opponents still have similar alternatives — so that panic buying doesn't set in.

articles.title: SEC Football Preview and Predictions for the 2026 Season
articles.summary: Is the SEC the nation's deepest conference? Absolutely, it should be once again. But is it the best? Well, anyone who says that would have a hard time backing it up.
articles.body:
Is the SEC the nation's deepest conference? Absolutely, it should be once again. But is it the best? Well, anyone who says that would have a hard time backing it up.

The Big Ten could just use the old playground comeback: "Scoreboard!"

The past three national champions all hail from that rival league to the north with Michigan, Ohio State, and last year's unbeaten Indiana Hoosiers hoisting the trophy. Before that run, the SEC had won 13 of the past 17 titles.

Now, though, the league with the most NFL talent year-in and year-out is looking to get back to the podium. It's not going to get any easier, either, with the conference moving to a nine-game schedule and the argument that the teams "just beat up on themselves" strengthening.

The SEC is, however, loaded with potentially elite teams once again. Texas, Georgia, Ole Miss and Texas A&M will be very good. Others like Oklahoma, LSU, Alabama, and possibly even Tennessee and South Carolina could be strong, too.

But can one of them reach the top? Let's take a look at what to expect from southern-fried football in '26.

It's impossible to zero in on just who is going to steal the show in the SEC. There's just so much talent, and it's an inexact science as last year's predictions of Garrett Nussmeier, DJ Lagway and LaNorris Sellers fell flat.

Sellers is back under center at South Carolina, and Arch Manning overcame a rough start a season ago at Texas to have a nice season, so both of those guys could flash. Georgia's Gunner Stockton , Oklahoma's John Mateer and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed are household-name field generals, and there are high hopes for Sam Leavitt at LSU.

But Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss is going to set the pace at quarterback, and Kewan Lacy forms one of the league's top offensive duos with the signal-caller.

Still, though, there are so many weapons across the league like runners Ahmad Hardy (Missouri), DeSean Bishop (Tennessee), Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown (Texas) and Jadan Baugh (Florida). Catching passes will be some of the nation's top weapons like Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo (Texas), Ryan Coleman-Williams (Alabama), TreyDez Green (LSU), Mario Craver (Texas A&M), Isaiah Satenga (Oklahoma), Braylon Staley and Mike Matthews (Tennessee) and Nyck Harbor (South Carolina).

Road-grading linemen include Trevor Goosby at Texas, Mizzou's Cayden Green, South Carolina's Jacarrius Peak , LSU's Jordan Seaton and returning Georgia standouts Earnest Greene III , Dontrell Glover and Drew Bobo . Tennessee's line should be strong, too, led by David Sanders Jr .

Defensive playmakers Colin Simmons and Rasheem Biles (Texas), Dylan Stewart (South Carolina), Princewill Umanmielen and Whit Weeks (LSU), Xavier Atkins (Auburn), DJ Hicks and Marcus Ratcliffe (Texas A&M), Arion Carter and Xavier Gilliam (Tennessee), Will Echoles and Suntarine Perkins (Ole Miss) will be elite.

Alabama ( Zabien Brown , Bray Hubbard , Keon Sabb ), Georgia ( KJ Bolden , Ellis Robinson IV , Khalil Barnes ), Oklahoma ( Eli Bowen and Peyton Bowen ) and LSU ( DJ Pickett , Ty Benefield ) have superstars in the secondary too.

Once again, the talent in the SEC is absurd.

Without a doubt, the biggest thing to watch this year is the league moving to nine conference games and how that will affect the title contenders.

Will they be more beat up? More prepared? Potentially, would an extra loss impact an SEC team that otherwise would have made the College Football Playoff with a cupcake win instead of the setback?

It's obviously a major money-maker for Greg Sankey and Co. to add the extra game, but the residual effects are at least worth monitoring.

OK, we know Lake Pontchartrain is 50 or so miles from Baton Rouge, but you get the point. Lane Kiffin left Ole Miss for hated rival LSU, and it's the biggest buzz in the league.

Everybody's got the Bayou Bengals' September 19 trip to Oxford on the schedule of must-watch TV, and Kiffin went out and added major reinforcements to the Tigers roster through the transfer portal and recruiting. Whether it's enough to turn LSU into an immediate contender remains to be seen.

The expectations are massive, though. When you make a move with these shockwaves, you want results right now. Everybody's watching.

Everybody's talking about Kiffin, of course. But this is the most turnover in the SEC coaching ranks in the modern era.

An astounding six teams changed head coaches – three of those coming from the AAC. Alex Golesh left South Florida for Auburn, Jon Sumrall exited Tulane for Florida and Ryan Silverfield headed up the road from Memphis to Arkansas.

Will Stein returns to his home state of Kentucky to coach the Wildcats, leaving his offensive coordinator perch at Oregon. And Pete Golding, who took over before the postseason run for the departed Kiffin, inherits a roster goldmine at Ole Miss.

Preseason prognostications indicate the league title could run through the Lone Star State.

Texas is deep, talented and the likely favorite in the league. Texas A&M is also coming off a playoff run and fortified some gaps through the transfer portal.

Georgia, Ole Miss, Oklahoma and others will have something to say about who's going to come out on top, but both of the SEC teams from Texas are loaded.

Several SEC teams will probably stake their hopes on youngsters at quarterback.

At Alabama, it's either going to be Keelon Russell or Austin Mack, so if Russell (a former 5-star redshirt freshman with very limited experience) wins the job, he'll be handed the keys to a potential title contender.

In the Volunteer State, it's going to be either true freshman Faizon Brandon or redshirt freshman George Macintyre calling the shots for Josh Heupel at Tennessee, and Vanderbilt likely will replace Diego Pavia with former 5-star true freshman Jared Curtis.

Then, at Florida, it's going to either be redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr., or Georgia Tech sophomore transfer Aaron Philo. Those are some good programs with uncertainty leading the way.

Tier 1: Texas, Georgia, Ole Miss, Texas A&M, LSU

The expected top five in the league are pretty clear right now, but everything after that is just a matter of how you think it's going to shake out. Also, if a couple of young quarterbacks hit in that second tier, things could change.

Texas is deep, and even though new defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has some turnover on that side of the ball, the Longhorns outfitted the roster through the portal with massive reinforcements.

At Georgia, titles are the benchmark, and coach Kirby Smart has a dynamic defense once again and a veteran quarterback in Gunner Stockton. He's won national titles with that same formula.

After last year's deep College Football Playoff run, folks in Oxford think this could be the year the Rebels break the SEC championship game drought, and oh what fun would that be in the first full year of the post-Lane Kiffin era? Speaking of Kiffin, he's got a roster at LSU built to win right now.

Texas A&M is kind of laying in the weeds with all this Longhorn buzz, but don't sleep on the Aggies, either. There are several teams in this group that can win it all.

Tier 2: Oklahoma, Alabama, South Carolina, Tennessee

Fans of two teams in this group aren't going to be happy to be here, and two others will be thrilled.

At Alabama, it's all about finding a viable running game and the right quarterback to lead Kalen DeBoer's offense. The defense is going to be one of the nation's best and terrific at all levels. But there have been offensive issues, and now they're replacing Ty Simpson? Questions abound.

Oklahoma made it to the playoffs a year ago with a magical run through a gauntlet schedule, and the Sooners return John Mateer at quarterback and playmakers on both sides of the ball. But can they catch magic twice? Sooners fans think they're a playoff lock.

For South Carolina and Tennessee, the season's a toss-up. The Vols have a lot to like on that roster if a young quarterback steps up. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has transformed things on that side of the ball.

In Columbia, it's now or never for Shane Beamer, but with LaNorris Sellers a prime pick for a rebound campaign with Kendal Briles calling the plays, a turnaround could be in the cards.

With six new coaches leading the charge in the league, there are really just a couple of coaches with warm bottoms entering the season.

Of course, if they have poor years, Tennessee's Josh Heupel and Alabama's Kalen DeBoer could possibly exit 2026 sweating a bit, but neither of those guys are in any danger of losing their jobs in the next calendar year. A couple of their peers are.

Last year, South Carolina was a College Football Playoff sleeper and crashed to a 4-8 record, winning just one SEC game and blowing a massive late-season lead against Texas A&M.

Now, after hiring Kendal Briles, Beamer, quarterback LaNorris Sellers and Co. are again on many minds as a possible turnaround team. The Gamecocks have talent, and they've got several opportunities to grab statement wins in the national spotlight.

If they don't, they'll be looking for a new coach. Beamer won't survive another losing season.

Mississippi State made it to a bowl game with a losing record a season ago and was promptly dismantled by Wake Forest. It was a disastrous end to a frustrating season.

Early on, the Bulldogs were the league's tough-luck loser.

After starting 4-0, MSU lost 41-34 at home against Tennessee in overtime, then after a lopsided loss to Texas A&M, fell 23-21 at Florida and took Texas to the brink in Starkville before losing 45-38 in overtime.

They fell apart after that, ending the year (following a close win over Arkansas) getting dismantled by Georgia, Missouri, Ole Miss and Wake Forest.

What does that mean for Lebby? He's coaching in a traditionally tough place to win. But 7-18 isn't going to cut it for long, and the Bulldogs aren't expected to make much noise this year, either.

Sep. 5: Clemson at LSU, Baylor vs. Auburn (in Atlanta)

Sep. 6: Louisville vs. Ole Miss (in Nashville)

Sep. 12: Oklahoma at Michigan, Tennessee at Georgia Tech, Ohio State at Texas, Arkansas at Utah

Nov. 28: Georgia Tech at Georgia, Louisville at Kentucky, South Carolina at Clemson

College football hits us with some nice little warmups during Week 1 to whet our appetites with Clemson traveling to LSU as well as Baylor meeting Auburn in Atlanta, and we'll know a bit about both sets of Tigers after those tilts. Louisville and Ole Miss meeting in Nashville is a sneaky showdown, too.

Everybody wants to watch Ohio State head to Austin to take on Texas in a rematch of national title contenders. Oklahoma heads to the Big House to face Michigan in another SEC/Big Ten showdown, and Tennessee travels to Atlanta to face Georgia Tech. Ryan Silverfield's first game at Arkansas will be in Salt Lake City against Utah in a tough test, too.

After those first two weekends, though, all we have in the way of marquee out-of-conference matchups is Florida State coming to Alabama in Week 3. Rivalry weekend gives us the next taste of non-SEC grudge matches.

Sep. 19: LSU at Ole Miss, Florida at Auburn

Sep. 26: Oklahoma at Georgia, Texas A&M at LSU, South Carolina at Alabama, Texas at Tennessee

Oct. 10: Georgia at Alabama, Texas A&M at Missouri, Texas vs. Oklahoma (Dallas)

Oct. 17: Missouri at Ole Miss, Alabama at Tennessee

Oct. 24: Ole Miss at Texas, Texas A&M at Alabama, Tennessee at South Carolina

Oct. 31: Florida vs. Georgia (Jacksonville)

Nov. 7: Georgia at Ole Miss, Texas at Missouri, Texas A&M at South Carolina, Alabama at LSU

Nov. 14: Missouri at Georgia, Texas at LSU, Tennessee at Texas A&M, Ole Miss at Oklahoma

Nov. 21: Georgia at South Carolina, Texas A&M at Oklahoma, LSU at Tennessee

Nov. 28: Oklahoma at Missouri, Auburn at Alabama

It's almost as if the SEC scheduling gods knew we simply couldn't wait.

Right off the bat on September 19, we've got the game we all want to see: Lane Kiffin heading back to Oxford as LSU coach to take on the Ole Miss team he built into a playoff program a season ago. That game will captivate the entire nation, but it's only the beginning.

The very next weekend may be the biggest of the year as the Sooners head to Athens, the Aggies descend on Death Valley, South Carolina gets tested right away in Tuscaloosa and Texas enters a hostile Neyland Stadium environment.

Following a bit of a "down" weekend October 3, Georgia plays at Alabama the next weekend, and we get the Red River Rivalry, too. In a nine-game schedule, there are no cakewalks, and that means high-quality games for us fans every single weekend.

If you love SEC football, you'll get a heaping helping of it this year. Game after game of intensity dot the calendar all the way through October and November.

The easiest answer here perhaps would be Ole Miss, which returns potentially the nation's top quarterback (Trinidad Chambliss) and running back (Kewan Lacy) along with plenty of capable pass-catchers.

But losing coach Lane Kiffin and offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. to LSU won't be easy to replace, so those growing pains the team could face adjusting to new play-caller John David Baker could stunt the potency a bit.

That's why we're rolling with Texas here.

Sure, a season ago, it took Arch Manning more than half the season to get going, but coach Steve Sarkisian went out in the transfer portal and surrounded his budding star signal-caller with elite talent in what is sure to be his final season in Austin.

The biggest prize for Texas is former Auburn receiver Cam Coleman who may be the most physically gifted receiver in the nation. He will team with Ryan Wingo for an elite 1-2 punch.

Beating Alabama for former North Carolina State running back Hollywood Smothers and pairing him with former Arizona State game-breaker Raleek Brown gives the Longhorns a top-tier running back duo, too.

Add in an offensive line with a lot of strong pieces, and Texas is going to score a bunch of points.

This is where the SEC could truly flex this year.

It wouldn't be surprising to see retooled Texas, which added players like Rasheem Biles to a roster that already featured Colin Simmons, an Alabama unit full of returning talent, a hard-nosed Texas A&M group taking on the persona of head coach Mike Elko or an Oklahoma group that led the league a year ago be the top defensive dog.

We're rolling with Georgia here, though.

The Bulldogs are going to have to replace a bunch of starts up front alongside Gabe Harris Jr., but the second and third levels of Glenn Schumann's defense will be nationally stout. Elijah Griffin is a potential All-American inside.

Georgia also has a deep and talented linebacking corps that features Raylen Wilson and Chris Cole, both of whom could be first-round picks. However, Quintavius Johnson has just as much talent at the Jack spot, too.

On the back end, KJ Bolden and Ellis Robinson IV also have the potential to be the best players in the nation at their position, and there are other veterans all over the place like Khalil Barnes and Demello Jones.

Projected SEC Championship: Texas vs. Ole Miss

This is the year the Ole Miss Rebels break the streak and make it to their first SEC championship game. Doing so in the wake of the Lane Kiffin era's abrupt end will be extra sweet, too.

Coach Pete Golding's team will be 10-2 heading into the conference title game, making it to the title game after beating their old coach and besting UGA on November 7 in a rematch of last year's playoff game.

Unfortunately for the Rebels, they won't be able to get past a Texas juggernaut clicking at the end of the season on both sides of the ball.

Everybody thought the Longhorns were going to compete for all the marbles a season ago, but an early-season struggle proved too much for them to overcome, and despite coach Steve Sarkisian's pleas, the College Football Playoff committee kept them out of the final 12.

That won't happen again this year. The 'Horns defense will be clicking under first-year coordinator Will Muschamp, and the offense will score enough to get by a strong Ole Miss team, propelling them to the playoffs.

Don't worry, Rebs. Your team is going, too.

Now, after hiring Kendal Briles, Beamer, quarterback LaNorris Sellers and Co. are again on many minds as a possible turnaround team. The Gamecocks have talent, and they've got several opportunities to grab statement wins in the national spotlight.
If they don't, they'll be looking for a new coach. Beamer won't survive another losing season.
Mississippi State made it to a bowl game with a losing record a season ago and was promptly dismantled by Wake Forest. It was a disastrous end to a frustrating season.
Early on, the Bulldogs were the league's tough-luck loser.

After starting 4-0, MSU lost 41-34 at home against Tennessee in overtime, then after a lopsided loss to Texas A&M, fell 23-21 at Florida and took Texas to the brink in Starkville before losing 45-38 in overtime.
They fell apart after that, ending the year (following a close win over Arkansas) getting dismantled by Georgia, Missouri, Ole Miss and Wake Forest.
What does that mean for Lebby? He's coaching in a traditionally tough place to win. But 7-18 isn't going to cut it for long, and the Bulldogs aren't expected to make much noise this year, either.
Sep. 5: Clemson at LSU, Baylor vs. Auburn (in Atlanta)
Sep. 6: Louisville vs. Ole Miss (in Nashville)
Sep. 12: Oklahoma at Michigan, Tennessee at Georgia Tech, Ohio State at Texas, Arkansas at Utah
Nov. 28: Georgia Tech at Georgia, Louisville at Kentucky, South Carolina at Clemson

College football hits us with some nice little warmups during Week 1 to whet our appetites with Clemson traveling to LSU as well as Baylor meeting Auburn in Atlanta, and we'll know a bit about both sets of Tigers after those tilts. Louisville and Ole Miss meeting in Nashville is a sneaky showdown, too.

Everybody wants to watch Ohio State head to Austin to take on Texas in a rematch of national title contenders. Oklahoma heads to the Big House to face Michigan in another SEC/Big Ten showdown, and Tennessee travels to Atlanta to face Georgia Tech. Ryan Silverfield's first game at Arkansas will be in Salt Lake City against Utah in a tough test, too.

After those first two weekends, though, all we have in the way of marquee out-of-conference matchups is Florida State coming to Alabama in Week 3. Rivalry weekend gives us the next taste of non-SEC grudge matches.
Sep. 19: LSU at Ole Miss, Florida at Auburn
Sep. 26: Oklahoma at Georgia, Texas A&M at LSU, South Carolina at Alabama, Texas at Tennessee
Oct. 10: Georgia at Alabama, Texas A&M at Missouri, Texas vs. Oklahoma (Dallas)
Oct. 17: Missouri at Ole Miss, Alabama at Tennessee
Oct. 24: Ole Miss at Texas, Texas A&M at Alabama, Tennessee at South Carolina
Oct. 31: Florida vs. Georgia (Jacksonville)
Nov. 7: Georgia at Ole Miss, Texas at Missouri, Texas A&M at South Carolina, Alabama at LSU
Nov. 14: Missouri at Georgia, Texas at LSU, Tennessee at Texas A&M, Ole Miss at Oklahoma
Nov. 21: Georgia at South Carolina, Texas A&M at Oklahoma, LSU at Tennessee
Nov. 28: Oklahoma at Missouri, Auburn at Alabama
It's almost as if the SEC scheduling gods knew we simply couldn't wait.

Right off the bat on September 19, we've got the game we all want to see: Lane Kiffin heading back to Oxford as LSU coach to take on the Ole Miss team he built into a playoff program a season ago. That game will captivate the entire nation, but it's only the beginning.

The very next weekend may be the biggest of the year as the Sooners head to Athens, the Aggies descend on Death Valley, South Carolina gets tested right away in Tuscaloosa and Texas enters a hostile Neyland Stadium environment.

Following a bit of a "down" weekend October 3, Georgia plays at Alabama the next weekend, and we get the Red River Rivalry, too. In a nine-game schedule, there are no cakewalks, and that means high-quality games for us fans every single weekend.
If you love SEC football, you'll get a heaping helping of it this year. Game after game of intensity dot the calendar all the way through October and November.

The easiest answer here perhaps would be Ole Miss, which returns potentially the nation's top quarterback (Trinidad Chambliss) and running back (Kewan Lacy) along with plenty of capable pass-catchers.

But losing coach Lane Kiffin and offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. to LSU won't be easy to replace, so those growing pains the team could face adjusting to new play-caller John David Baker could stunt the potency a bit.
That's why we're rolling with Texas here.

Sure, a season ago, it took Arch Manning more than half the season to get going, but coach Steve Sarkisian went out in the transfer portal and surrounded his budding star signal-caller with elite talent in what is sure to be his final season in Austin.
The biggest prize for Texas is former Auburn receiver Cam Coleman who may be the most physically gifted receiver in the nation. He will team with Ryan Wingo for an elite 1-2 punch.

Beating Alabama for former North Carolina State running back Hollywood Smothers and pairing him with former Arizona State game-breaker Raleek Brown gives the Longhorns a top-tier running back duo, too.
Add in an offensive line with a lot of strong pieces, and Texas is going to score a bunch of points.
This is where the SEC could truly flex this year.

It wouldn't be surprising to see retooled Texas, which added players like Rasheem Biles to a roster that already featured Colin Simmons, an Alabama unit full of returning talent, a hard-nosed Texas A&M group taking on the persona of head coach Mike Elko or an Oklahoma group that led the league a year ago be the top defensive dog.
We're rolling with Georgia here, though.

The Bulldogs are going to have to replace a bunch of starts up front alongside Gabe Harris Jr., but the second and third levels of Glenn Schumann's defense will be nationally stout. Elijah Griffin is a potential All-American inside.

Georgia also has a deep and talented linebacking corps that features Raylen Wilson and Chris Cole, both of whom could be first-round picks. However, Quintavius Johnson has just as much talent at the Jack spot, too.

On the back end, KJ Bolden and Ellis Robinson IV also have the potential to be the best players in the nation at their position, and there are other veterans all over the place like Khalil Barnes and Demello Jones.
Projected SEC Championship: Texas vs. Ole Miss
This is the year the Ole Miss Rebels break the streak and make it to their first SEC championship game. Doing so in the wake of the Lane Kiffin era's abrupt end will be extra sweet, too.

Coach Pete Golding's team will be 10-2 heading into the conference title game, making it to the title game after beating their old coach and besting UGA on November 7 in a rematch of last year's playoff game.
Unfortunately for the Rebels, they won't be able to get past a Texas juggernaut clicking at the end of the season on both sides of the ball.

Everybody thought the Longhorns were going to compete for all the marbles a season ago, but an early-season struggle proved too much for them to overcome, and despite coach Steve Sarkisian's pleas, the College Football Playoff committee kept them out of the final 12.

That won't happen again this year. The 'Horns defense will be clicking under first-year coordinator Will Muschamp, and the offense will score enough to get by a strong Ole Miss team, propelling them to the playoffs.
Don't worry, Rebs. Your team is going, too.

articles.title: Soccer Fans Launch Global Petition Urging FIFA Boss Infantino to Resign over World Cup 'Betrayal'
articles.summary: GENEVA (AP) — A collection of soccer fan groups from around the world launched a petition Thursday calling for Gianni Infantino to resign as FIFA president after he tried to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.
articles.body:
GENEVA (AP) — A collection of soccer fan groups from around the world launched a petition Thursday calling for Gianni Infantino to resign as FIFA president after he tried to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

The petition with the hashtag InfantinOut also calls for FIFA "to be rebuilt so that the current debacle can never happen again."

"The shameful attempt by one individual — the FIFA President himself — to sell off the World Cup to private investors exposed a betrayal football will never forget," the petition said about Infantino's plan for a commercial spinoff, which he dropped amid a furious backlash.

The fan groups include Football Supporters Europe, Football Supporters Africa and, in North America, the Independent Supporters Council, plus about 40 national fan groups worldwide.

Infantino has resisted calls to leave office despite European soccer body UEFA saying it has no confidence in him. He has also been criticized by the leadership of North America's CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation.

Some of FIFA's 211 member federations are supporting Infantino, including 2030 World Cup co-host Morocco as well as Qatar, where he lived before the emirate hosted the 2022 World Cup, and Lebanon, which gave him citizenship this year. Saudi Arabia, the 2034 host, has not publicly backed Infantino despite his close political ties to the kingdom.

"Gianni Infantino has demonstrated a profound failure of leadership, incompatible with democratic governance," the fan petition states. "The concentration of power around the FIFA Presidency, combined with opaque decision-making, personality cult clientelism, and zero accountability has destroyed any remaining trust in the world governing body."

"For the credibility of FIFA — and for the future of the game — he must resign," the petition adds.

FIFA was approached for comment about the petition.

The petition also cites Infantino's past support for projects that outraged fans, including the failed European Super League project, pushing to hold World Cups every two years that was resisted and the "extortionate ticketing policy at the 2026 FIFA World Cup."

FIFA and Infantino did not consult with fan groups before setting record ticket prices for the 104-game tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, that provoked anger and led to some tickets being sold for $60 to the most loyal fans of each of the 48 teams.

Football Supporters Europe is the official liaison for fans with UEFA and advises on ticket prices for European Championships and club cup finals like the Champions League.

articles.title: Peyton Manning's Son Marshall Makes HSFB Debut, Watch 2030 QB Complete 1st Pass in Trending Video
articles.summary: The son of an NFL legend made his high school football debut on Thursday.
articles.body:
The son of an NFL legend made his high school football debut on Thursday.

Marshall Manning, the son of Peyton Manning, is a freshman at Baylor School in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and got a few snaps during the second quarter of their season opener against Brentwood Academy.

HS football team snaps 101-game losing streak

Manning, who wears the same No. 16 his father wore at Tennessee, is looking to put together a strong high school career and eventually reach the collegiate level, but it could be a while before he gets regular snaps.

He's currently serving as the backup quarterback to Keegan Croucher, a 4-star senior who is committed to Ole Miss.

Once Croucher leaves in the spring, Manning could have the reins to the Baylor offense as a sophomore.

Manning has the chance to continue the tremendous legacy of his family. His grandfather, Archie, played quarterback at Ole Miss before going on to have an NFL career that featured two Pro Bowl selections.

His father is one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, winning five MVPs, a pair of Super Bowls and countless other accolades before retiring in 2016.

Manning's uncle Eli also had a strong career, winning two Super Bowls and two Super Bowl MVPs. He retired in 2019.

The next generation of the Manning family features not only Marshall, but his cousin Arch, who is coming off a strong first season as Texas' starter and is an early favorite to win the Heisman Trophy and go first overall in next year's NFL draft.

It's safe to say Marshall has plenty of people in his circle who know how to succeed at a high level, but for now, he'll wait his turn as a backup.
