articles.title: Marlaska ordena investigar a los Policías que cargaron contra aficionados del Barcelona
articles.standfirst: La Delegación de Gobierno en la Comunitat Valenciana niega que se requisaran esteladas en el Elche-Barça
articles.summary: La Delegación de Gobierno en la Comunitat Valenciana, mientras, niega que se requisaran esteladas en el Elche-Barça
articles.body: Fernando Grande-Marlaska, ministro del Interior, ha ordenado, según el diario El Mundo, investigar a los Policías que cargaron contra aficionados del Barcelona en el partido de este domingo contra el Elche. Además, la Delegación del Gobierno en la Comunitat Valenciana ha informado también este lunes de que ha abierto una investigación interna en la Policía Nacional sobre la actuación de los agentes y desmintió que se requisase ninguna bandera estelada por parte de los policías que intervinieron.  Junts, ERC y la CUP denunciaron este lunes la actuación de agentes de la Policía Nacional contra seguidores del Barcelona en la previa del encuentro, en la que un hincha fue golpeado por varios policías, según imágenes difundidas en las redes sociales. El vídeo muestra cómo agentes de la Policía Nacional golpearon a un joven tras arrebatarle una estelada, que permanece en manos de uno de los policías durante toda la escena. El joven se encaró con los policías y estos terminaron golpeándole con las porras en el suelo. El Barcelona también condenó el uso "desproporcionado" de la fuerza por parte de la Policía, lamentó que, "una vez más", agentes policiales "requisaran banderas esteladas a aficionados azulgranas" y se puso a disposición del seguidor detenido y de su familia "para ofrecerles el apoyo que puedan necesitar".

articles.title: El Valencia hace oficial la cesión de Kayne Van Oevelen
articles.standfirst: El portero del Ipswich Town espera ser inscrito en la Liga para poder entrar en la convocatoria del partido contra el Betis
articles.summary: El portero del Ipswich Town espera ser inscrito en la Liga para poder entrar en la convocatoria del partido contra el Betis
articles.body: El Valencia ha anunciado oficialmente el fichaje de Kayne Van Oevelen, que se incorpora al conjunto de Mestalla en calidad de cedido procedente del Ipswich Town hasta el final de la temporada 2026-27. El acuerdo no contempla opción de compra y refuerza una de las posiciones que la dirección deportiva consideraba prioritarias en el actual mercado estival. A sus 23 años, el guardameta neerlandés llega para competir por un puesto en la portería valencianista junto a Stole Dimitrievski y su incorporación supone además el sexto movimiento del club durante el presente verano. De hecho, el Valencia espera que el trámite para la inscripción en la Liga se cierre mañana y podría entrar en la convocatoria. Van Oevelen aterrizó en Valencia el domingo 23 de agosto para completar los trámites previos a la oficialización de la operación. A su llegada al aeropuerto de Manises, el portero mostró su satisfacción por incorporarse a la entidad blanquinegra.  El meta nacido en Zaandam se formó en el fútbol neerlandés y dio el salto al primer plano con el Volendam, donde llamó la atención por sus condiciones físicas, especialmente sus casi dos metros de estatura, su dominio del juego aéreo y su capacidad para ocupar espacios bajo palos. Durante la pasada temporada disputó 32 encuentros ligueros y se consolidó como una de las apariciones más destacadas de la Eredivisie, despertando el interés de varios clubes europeos. El Valencia ya había seguido de cerca al guardameta cuando militaba en el Volendam e incluso exploró su incorporación en propiedad antes de que el Ipswich Town cerrara su traspaso este verano. Apenas unas semanas después de llegar al conjunto inglés, la falta de perspectivas inmediatas de minutos en la Premier League abrió la puerta a una cesión que finalmente se ha concretado con destino Mestalla.

articles.title: Las inscripciones relámpago del Levante
articles.standfirst: Hasta cinco jugadores fueron dados de alta en la competición en la tarde de este lunes
articles.summary: Hasta cinco jugadores fueron dados de alta en la competición en la tarde de este lunes
articles.body: De manera relámpago, el Levante inscribió hasta cinco jugadores para poder estar disponibles en la lista de Luís Castro para enfrentarse a Club Atlético Osasuna, correspondiente a la segunda jornada de liga. La salida de Kareem Tunde al West Bromwich Albion, aún sin ser oficial, facilitó la difícil situación que el club del barrio de Orriols está teniendo para poder dar de alta a las diferentes incorporaciones de este mercado de fichajes. El primero que la propia competición mostró fue al central austriaco Ifeanyi Ndukwe, que no consiguió debutar en competición oficial a causa de tan solo ejercitarse con el grupo durante dos sesiones de entrenamiento. Así mismo, otro de los jugadores que también figuran en LaLiga es Dani Requena, aunque tampoco pudo lucir la camiseta granota en el Sadar. Por otro lado, dos de las incorporaciones de este verano y que también fueron inscritos en la previa ante Osasuna fueron Thiago Fernández, que fue titular en la segunda fecha del torneo, y Hugo Sotelo, aunque tan solo estuvo presente durante dos minutos del envite. El caso más llamativo de todos fue el de Musuayi. El atacante belga fue dado de alta e incluso, inicialmente figuraba en la lista de convocados del entrenador luso aunque, un cambio de última hora, debido a una sanción del pasado lo apartó definitivamente del choque.

articles.title: Luís Castro: "El resultado es justo, pero si hubiera ganado un equipo, hubiéramos sido nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador luso ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha matizado que, la ausencia de Musuayi, se debe a una sanción del pasado
articles.summary: El entrenador luso ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha matizado que, la ausencia de Musuayi, se debe a una sanción del pasado
articles.body: Luís Castro se ha marchado con mejores sensaciones con la que se marchó del RCDE Stadium la semana pasada. El técnico luso ha calificado que la imagen del equipo "es otra cosa. Hemos tenido las oportunidades más claras y hemos tenido identidad". Así mismo, el portugués ha confirmado la salida de Kareem Tunde y ha dejado abierta la posibilidad de otras ventas de la plantilla y la factible incorporación de alguna cara nueva, "siempre y cuando mejoren al equipo".  Un Levante competitivo, diferente al del Espanyol: "Es otra cosa. Jugamos fuera, en un campo muy difícil, y has peleado para intentar ganar. Las oportunidades más claras han sido nuestras y hemos tenido identidad. Mejorando un poco las situaciones tácticas y los jugadores que han venido, cuando estén más tiempo, mejorará todo" Jugadores inscritos sin minutos: "Thiago ha jugado titular y no estaba inscrito. El equipo estaba bien y los cambios los hemos hecho para refrescar. Estábamos en el campo adversario y ellos estaban haciendo balones largos. Estábamos entrenado en el área y con más situaciones ofensivas que ellos. Por eso no hemos hecho cambios. El equipo estaba bien, pero los que han llegado necesitan tiempo para estar con nosotros" Kareem Tunde: "Yo pienso que saldrá. No sé si está confirmado, pero saldrá. No estoy muy preocupado de eso" Empate justo: "El resultado es justo y pienso que, si hubiera ganado un equipo, lo hubiéramos ganado nosotros. Pero el resultado es justo. Ellos también han tenido algunas situaciones, pero pienso que las más claras la hemos tenido nosotros" Musuayi, sanción del pasado: "No ha jugado por una expulsión, pero no lo comprendo. Él ha tenido una expulsión y después de haber estado suspendido, pero ha jugado en Bélgica. Yo no comprendo eso. Después de la suspensión, ha jugado, y ahora no puedo. Yo no comprendo eso. Si juegas en competición y ahora está sancionado, yo no comprendo esto. Yo lo quería tener en el banquillo porque es un jugador que ha trabajado muy bien" Actuación de Osasuna: "Es un equipo que tiene calidad. Individualmente son muy fuertes y los delanteros tienen mucha calidad. Colectivamente crecerá. En algunos momentos del partido nos han hecho daño y creo que es un equipo que tendrá un campeonato normal" Necesidades futbolísticas ante la marcha de Kareem: "En primer lugar, tenemos el fair play financiero que no ayuda. El club está dando la vida para encontrar soluciones. Si tenemos oportunidades, hasta que no termine el mercado estamos abiertos, pero fichar jugadores por fichar, no queremos. Dependemos de la liga y el fair play. Estamos contentos por Kareem que ha trabajado muy bien y lo merece" Posible venta de Carlos Álvarez: "Todos pueden salir. Carlos no ha tenido minutos porque yo lo he decidido. Necesitábamos otras cosas para el partido de hoy, pero todos los jugadores del Levante y yo también, estamos preparados para salir. Yo es una situación de uno u otro. El mercado está abierto. Si hay ofertas buenas, puede salir uno u otro"

articles.title: Aubameyang, el salvavidas del Dépor
articles.standfirst: Gracias a sus goles le sirven al Depor sumar dos puntos y seguir sin perder
articles.summary: Gracias a sus goles le sirven al Depor sumar dos puntos y seguir sin perder
articles.body: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang es un fichaje de muchos kilates para un Deportivo que vuelve a Primera tras ocho temporadas sin jugar en la máxima categoría. Para el deportivismo es ya un ídolo y un ejemplo para el resto de la plantilla. Tras más de 400 goles en toda su carrera el internacional gabonés lleva dos goles en los dos primeros partidos con la camiseta blanquiazul. Dos goles que suman los dos puntos que tiene el Dépor en su casillero. Desde Bebeto no marcaba un jugador debutante en los dos primeros partidos de Liga. Aubameyang ha llegado a La Coruña para triunfar y para ayudar al equipo a conseguir la salvación. Dentro de la plantilla ya ejerce de capitán y no para de ayudar a los futbolistas más jóvenes. Para el ex del Marsella es muy bonito el cariño que le está mostrando toda la ciudad. “Me han recibido muy bien y estoy encantado con llegar a un equipo que ya lo conocía desde que comencé en Alemania”, comentaba el ‘7’ gallego. En su presentación el delantero fue muy claro. “Vengo a hacer goles, a dar asistencias y sobre todo a ganar muchos partidos”, expresaba hace unos días.

articles.title: Reencuentro con abrazo cariñoso entre Arbeloa y Xabi Alonso
articles.standfirst: Vuelven a verse tras el cambio de papeles en el Real Madrid la pasada temporada
articles.summary: Vuelven a verse tras el cambio de papeles en el Real Madrid la pasada temporada
articles.body: El Fulham-Chelsea dejó una imagen esperadísima: la del reencuentro de Xabi Alonso y Álvaro Arbeloa. Dos entrenadores españoles que compartieron vestuario durante muchos años en varios equipos y que el año pasado protagonizaron un relevo sonado en el banquillo del Real Madrid, cuando el club blanco despidió al ahora entrenador del Chelsea y ascendió a Arbeloa al primer equipo. Coincidieron en Liverpool, Real Madrid y selección española. Juntos jugaron un total de 262 partidos y conquistaron ligas, Champions, Eurocopa y Mundial. Sin embargo, uno de los clubes que los unió, el Real Madrid, abrió una grieta entre ellos por el apresurado despido de Xabi. A final de temporada, Arbeloa también tuvo que marcharse del Bernabéu y ambos han tenido que buscarse la vida en la Premier, concretamente en clubes de Londres. La cercanía ha provocado que su relación vuelva a ser cercana, puesto que sus familias se conocen bien y la cordialidad entre ambos nunca desapareció. El abrazo y las muestras de cariño mutuas en la banda durante el encuentro deja claro que la relación entre dos de los técnicos españoles que este año compiten en la Premier es amistosa.

articles.standfirst: Partido correspondiente a la primera jornada liguera que fue aplazado por los mundialistas
articles.summary: Partido correspondiente a la primera jornada liguera que fue aplazado por los mundialistas
articles.body: Valencia y Betis se enfrentan hoy martes 25 de agosto de 2026 desde las 21.00 horas en el Estadio de Mestalla en el partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de LaLiga EA Sports que fue aplazado en su día después de que el argentino Giovani Lo Celso alcanzara la final del Mundial con su selección, y tras solicitud por parte de los verdiblancos. Una cita en la que ambos conjuntos tratarán de seguir sumando en la clasificación. El equipo de Carlos Corberán estrenó su temporada en partido oficial empatando sin goles, también en Mestalla, frente al Celta de Vigo. Sin De Haas, Copete, Diego López, Canós y Foulquier, con refuerzos pendientes a una semana del cierre del mercado, un ambiente enrarecido en su estadio y con las quejas de su técnico por el menor descanso de su equipo, los valencianistas tratarán de hacerse fuertes en casa para firmar su primer triunfo de la temporada. Los de Pellegrini, por su parte, lograron imponerse el pasado viernes por 1-0 a la Real Sociedad en el Estadio de La Cartuja, para comenzar el curso sumando tres puntos. Para su visita a la capital del Turia incorporan al delantero irlandés Troy Parrott, su último fichaje hasta la fecha en el mercado, pero siguen sin poder contar por distintos problemas físicos con Diego Conde, Aitor Ruibal, Giovani Lo Celso, Ez Abde, José Antonio Morante y Gonzalo Petit. El partido entre Valencia y Real Betis de la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports se juega el martes 25 de agosto a las 21:00 horas. El partido entre Valencia y Betis de la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través del canal DAZN. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El Valencia llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Betis tras empatar sin goles (0-0) contra el Celta. Ahora mismo el conjunto che se encuentra en la 11ª posición de la clasificación con un punto. El Betis llega al partido de LaLiga EA Sports contra el Valencia tras ganar a la Real Sociedad (1-0). El conjunto verdiblanco se encuentra en la 7ª posición de la clasificación con tres puntos.

articles.title: Ferguson? Guardiola? Mourinho? Ranking the best managers in Premier League history
articles.summary: Thirteen managers have won the Premier League title, but which of them will make it into our top 10 covering the competition's history?
articles.body:
When it comes to ranking managers, titles are a good place to start.

Only four bosses have won more than one since the Premier League era began in 1992. So if you do some quick maths, you'll probably not be surprised by the names that top this list.

But there is a debate to be had around where they should rank, and who else makes it into the top 10. So let's have it.

You can rank your greatest managers of the Premier League era below too.

Longevity deserves a mention here. Take David Moyes, for example, racking up 755 games in Premier League dugouts - only Arsene Wenger (828) and Sir Alex Ferguson (810) have more.

Naturally, Moyes has the third-most wins in Premier League history too, although his 291 across spells with Everton, Manchester United, Sunderland and West Ham fall some way short of Wenger's 476 at Arsenal and Ferguson's 528 at United.

Pep Guardiola is also on Scotsman Moyes' shoulder despite managing barely half as many games.

Harry Redknapp has the fourth-most games under his belt (641), fifth-most wins (236) and also completes the top five for goals scored (818).

We should talk about win percentage too, and the former Tottenham manager who really deserves a shout here is Mauricio Pochettino, who guided Spurs to their best-ever Premier League finish of second in 2016-17 and also coached Southampton and Chelsea.

The Argentine is the only manager - of those who have coached more than 100 games - to have not lifted the title yet still won more than half his games throughout his Premier League career.

But really, to make this list, you have to have won a Premier League title. In total, 13 managers have done so. Meaning three are getting left at the door.

Arne Slot of Liverpool is the first to be cut. The others are a hard choice.

Manuel Pellegrini's Manchester City record was impressive before the Chilean made way for Guardiola. During those three years, plus 17 months at West Ham, his average of 1.92 goals per game ranks fifth among all managers with a century of matches.

But he spent big at the Hammers only to then endure a desperate run of form - so the man known as the Engineer, the only manager from outside Europe to win the title, misses out.

As does Antonio Conte, who had boom and bust spells at Chelsea and Spurs.

Instead, the pair are pipped by the only boss to win the title in all of Europe's top five leagues.

10. Carlo Ancelotti. Title winner 2009-10

AC Milan, Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain, Real Madrid and, of course, Chelsea.

King Carlo has steered them all to domestic glory, not to mention his Champions League record of five successes. Yet his initial tenure in the English top flight was fleeting.

The Italian blitzed his way to the Premier League crown at the first time of asking at Stamford Bridge. But, after snapping up Fernando Torres for a then-British record fee from Liverpool the following January, Ancelotti was swiftly shown the door after Chelsea finished as runners-up in his second season.

A surprising return to England came via the Everton dugout, where Ancelotti delivered successive mid-table finishes before Real Madrid came calling.

Earlier this year, Mikel Arteta became the 13th manager to win the Premier League but the first Arsenal boss to do so since Arsene Wenger in 2004.

The Spaniard also snapped an eight-year run of either Manchester City or Liverpool winning the trophy.

Bursting clear of his rivals like they were a technical area, Arteta shrugged off questions over his team's sometimes robust style as well as those who suggested the Gunners were destined to always be runners-up.

As the only current Premier League boss to have won the title, and with Arsenal adding to an already stacked squad this summer, you wouldn't bet against the former playmaker creeping further up this list in future.

8. Roberto Mancini. Title winner 2011-12

Premier League titles don't come more dramatic than two goals in added time - including a 94th-minute winner - on the final day of the season, especially to clinch a first top-flight crown in more than 40 years while denying your arch-rivals.

Roberto Mancini got Manchester City's lavish new era rolling by winning the FA Cup in his first full season, having replaced Mark Hughes in December 2009, and followed up with the title before he was sacked the following summer.

The Italian, though, stacks up well, boasting the fourth-best points-per-game tally for any boss to have managed at least 100 Premier League games - coming in just above Conte and Jose Mourinho - and the fifth-best win percentage.

Meanwhile, his City stars make the top five for goals per game and boast the best record for fewest goals conceded, a miserly 0.83 per game.

Kenny Dalglish's greatest success as a boss came at Liverpool before the Premier League era began, winning three titles in four seasons, initially as a player-manager, before he departed in February 1991 after almost 15 years with the club.

He wound up at second-tier Blackburn Rovers eight months later and immediately steered them into the Premier League via the play-offs.

Bankrolled by local businessman Jack Walker, Rovers snapped up Alan Shearer from Southampton for a British record fee of Â£3.6m and then finished fourth and second before overcoming Manchester United to win the title in 1995.

That made Dalglish only the fourth manager to win the English top flight with two different clubs.

Dalglish was unable to repeat the trick at Newcastle, although they finished runners-up in both the league and FA Cup during his tenure, while his return to Liverpool ended in 2012 after League Cup success but an eighth-placed finish.

6. Claudio Ranieri. Title winner 2015-16

Dilly ding, dilly dong. Ranieri rides into the top six on pure vibes. The man behind the 5,000-1 miracle. The one who turned a cast of footballing misfits into an all-conquering force. The father of Leicester City's Premier League triumph.

That is worth his entry alone. Yet, in what seems another lifetime, the Tinkerman almost got his hands on a winner's medal more than a decade earlier.

Buoyed by the first wave of Roman Abramovich spending, Ranieri steered Chelsea to second in 2004, only behind Arsenal's Invincibles.

Chelsea probably should have won the Champions League too, losing in the semi-finals to Monaco, but that became a defining moment for the man who would replace him.

Jurgen Klopp is in some ways the Andy Murray of the Premier League. All action, high-octane performances, adored by his fans yet prickly under pressure. He enjoyed incredible success but would probably have dominated more were it not for a generational opponent.

In this rather stretched analogy, Manchester City are Klopp's Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. If it had not been for his Catalan counterpart down the M62, Klopp's rock 'n' roll Reds would have been the undoubted top dogs under the German.

Instead, they racked up more than 90 points on three occasions and 'only' clinched one title in 2019-20 - it was, however, Liverpool's first in 30 years and their first of the Premier League era.

4. Jose Mourinho. Title winner 2004-05, 05-06 & 14-15

Lungs still pumping from that touchline sprint at Old Trafford, Jose Mourinho landed at Chelsea days after guiding Porto to a remarkable Champions League triumph and declared himself a 'Special One'.

Taking the baton from Ranieri and armed with a host of new signings, the Portuguese enigma stormed the title in his first season - Chelsea winning the league by 12 points, conceding only 15 goals and ruffling the raincoats of Wenger and Ferguson.

Mourinho backed it up in his second season before relationships began to fray and the most successful boss in the club's history left in September 2007. Mourinho, though, had transformed the Blues into a formidable force.

He returned six years later, after titles in Milan and Madrid, and clinched his third Premier League crown in his second season, only to be gone by Christmas of the following campaign.

Box-office spells followed at Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur, but they came nowhere near the success of his time in south-west London.

3. Arsene Wenger. Title winner 1997-98, 2001-02 & 03-04

It's fine margins between Wenger and Mourinho, as both their arrivals brought the dawn of new eras in the Premier League.

Indeed, Mourinho once said Wenger is a "specialist in failure", but in this list the Frenchman just pips his rival thanks to engineering the only 'Invincibles' season in Premier League history.

Wenger, joining from Japanese outfit Nagoya Grampus Eight, was deemed a curious choice at first but professionalised Arsenal and led them to league titles in 1998, 2002 and - the piece de resistance - that unbeaten season of 2003-04.

That he was unable to win another title in the 14 years that followed perhaps tarnishes Wenger's legacy slightly, but the Arsenal team he built during his first decade was one of the best the Premier League ever witnessed.

2. Pep Guardiola. Title winner 2017-18, 18-19, 20-21, 21-22, 22-23 & 23-24

Talking of managers who changed the face of English football, no-one has moved the game right from the elite level through to grassroots as much as Pep Guardiola.

Blame the Catalan for Sunday League goalkeepers playing out from the back.

And to think there were question marks over whether Guardiola's style - honed at Barcelona - would work in the more robust English game.

Guardiola was, of course, lavishly backed in the transfer market, but his Manchester City side won titles at a prolific rate.

City became the first English men's side to win four in a row - they landed six Premier League titles in total during Pep's decade in charge, as well as notching a century of points in 2018.

1. Sir Alex Ferguson. Title winner 1992-93, 93-94, 95-96, 96-97, 98-99, 99-2000, 2000-01, 02-03, 06-07, 07-08, 08-09, 10-11, 12-13

The first two decades of the Premier League were dominated by one man.

Sir Alex Ferguson won 13 titles and was able to continuously rebuild his side in order to keep Manchester United at the top of English football - from Eric Cantona to the '99 Treble winners, and later that front three of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and Carlos Tevez.

Even after Ronaldo left for Real Madrid in 2009, and Tevez defected to the other side of Manchester, Ferguson continued winning titles until he retired in 2013.

His record title haul is more than double any manager from any era of men's English top-flight football, not just the Premier League - Guardiola, Liverpool's Bob Paisley and George Ramsay for Aston Villa are next on the list on six.

It makes Fergie the undoubted number one.

articles.title: How did record nine new managers fare in opening round of Premier League games?
articles.summary: Who impressed and who has work to do? BBC Sport chief football writer Phil McNulty looks at how the nine new managerial appointments fared on the opening week of the Premier League season.
articles.body:
Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the season with new managers.

The post-Pep Guardiola era has begun at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca, while Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot. Xabi Alonso is the latest with his foot in the revolving door of managers at Chelsea .

So how did the new faces fare after an eventful first weekend of the new campaign?

The German successor to Iraola came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City , only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.

Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.

Not a bad start to take the lead after 31 seconds and a satisfactory start to Alonso's reign, but there was obvious good and obvious bad in what he watched at Craven Cottage.

The attacking triumvirate of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and newcomer Morgan Rogers hit the ground running, all scoring and combining to devastating effect.

Equally devastating to Chelsea 's Premier League chances and the Alonso revival could be the failure to find a better goalkeeper than the unreliable Robert Sanchez, who was at fault for both Fulham goals.

Alonso must find an answer quickly otherwise what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers give with one hand Sanchez could take away with both hands.

Tactically Alonso used a back three with Reece James operating in midfield but also dropping back into defence.

Disappointing start for the highly-regarded Sage, who did such an outstanding job at Lens, with defeat at Everton but he also knows the outcome could have been a much more satisfactory one.

Palace's second half display will have disappointed him, but they had chances in the opening period to set up their first win at Everton since 2014. They hit the woodwork twice, while Jean-Phillipe Mateta was wasteful. Sage and his team paid a heavy price.

Sage's unhappy opening weekend will not have been helped by a contract row surrounding striker Mateta that puts his future in question, while he will want more numbers and quality to add to his squad.

Next up Manchester City at Selhurst Park, where Sage will sample the superb night game atmosphere as he searches for his first league win. No easy task.

Tough opener and conceding within the first minute did not help Arbeloa's cause as he builds after taking over from Marco Silva.

It is already clear he needs to make sure Fulham can find some goals, although he will be delighted young debutant Gonzalo Garcia got off the mark. It was more of a struggle for another new arrival from Real Madrid, Cesar Palacios.

The jewel in Arbeloa's crown will be 19-year-old Josh King, who he described as "unbelievable". It is already clear the youngster will bear a heavy weight of responsibility under Fulham 's new management.

Ipswich Town have backed Kieran McKenna's successor with big money in the transfer market, Â£150m on a dozen signings, and Gary O'Neil was rewarded with a vital victory against Sunderland .

O'Neil may just be the beneficiary from lessons learned during Ipswich's last spell in the Premier League, when they took 11 games to get a win and went down with a whimper with just 22 points.

He will have been delighted with the impact of Julio Enciso, who he worked with at Strasbourg, and his early partnership with Brazilian striker Emersonn, the pair combining superbly for the latter's opening goal.

Plenty still to work on but O'Neil looked in the mood to enjoy his cup of tea and bar of chocolate while watching Match Of The Day on Saturday night.

Iraola was spared the ignominy of defeat in his first Premier League game since succeeding Arne Slot by Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th minute penalty â but this was a sobering fact-finding mission for the new man in charge at Anfield.

He did not seem unduly concerned, but both Newcastle United 's goals will have been hauntingly familiar to those who watched Liverpool 's title defence collapse under Slot last season.

Newcastle cashed in on Liverpool 's wide open midfield, a flaw from the last campaign that saw them so vulnerable to fast counter-attacks. Anthony Elanga sliced through Liverpool for the first then six of Iraola's team stood idly by as Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock combined for the second.

Iraola has suggested Liverpool will not strengthen in midfield with a 'number 6' type defensively-minded player. This early evidence (not to mention what was seen last season) suggests he should.

If not, the draw at Newcastle was a red flag showing Iraola needs to find an internal solution which is not currently obvious.

It's all very well targeting wide players such as Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh, but what about when teams are running straight through the heart of Liverpool 's team?

Iraola must also find a way to make the subdued Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz look like the players Liverpool paid Â£241m for. Both were poor again at St. James' Park.

It looked like it was going to be a losing start for Guardiola's successor before Manchester City pulled it around with two late goals to beat Bournemouth .

How Maresca needed it after City were pounded by Arsenal in the Community Shield. The Italian's emotions at the final whistle looked as much relief as celebration. He needs wins just to settle post-Guardiola nerves and ease the transition.

Maresca described the day as "perfect". It very nearly wasn't.

Erling Haaland's crop is not the only new look at City this season, but on occasions there were passages of play with lots of possession but little punch, a familiar pattern from Maresca's time at Leicester City and Chelsea . The use of Marc Guehi in midfield was a tactical twist.

Maresca will have wanted the win, no matter how it came, and City achieved it, even though it did carry a lot of the hallmarks of a work in progress.

Seconds away from what would have been a very significant win against Liverpool , but still plenty for Jaissle to take away even with the concession of that late, late penalty.

The Toon Army were right behind the new manager and his team, reshaping after the loss of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, and they responded with real intensity.

The effort was there, the attacking style Jaissle wants was there, only the win was missing but enough to please him after fall-out from this summer's Tyneside turbulence.

Poor start for the Austrian who brought FA Cup and Europa League success to Crystal Palace , losing 1-0 to a late Leeds United goal at The City Ground.

Glasner claimed he cannot simply lay hands on players and they perform like "Real Madrid in the 70s", but this still was an unsatisfactory opening as he tries to bring stability and success to Nottingham Forest and their demanding owner Evangelos Marinkis after four managers were in charge last season.

He had no new signings in his starting line-up, with eight from Nuno Espirito Santo's team in the opening-day win over Brentford last season, although it looks like striker Liam Delap might arrive from Chelsea .

Every Forest manager needs wins (and very quickly) so to make a losing introduction was a real blow for Glasner.
paragraphs: Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the season with new managers.

The post-Pep Guardiola era has begun at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca, while Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot. Xabi Alonso is the latest with his foot in the revolving door of managers at Chelsea .
So how did the new faces fare after an eventful first weekend of the new campaign?
The German successor to Iraola came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City , only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.
Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.
Not a bad start to take the lead after 31 seconds and a satisfactory start to Alonso's reign, but there was obvious good and obvious bad in what he watched at Craven Cottage.
The attacking triumvirate of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and newcomer Morgan Rogers hit the ground running, all scoring and combining to devastating effect.

Equally devastating to Chelsea 's Premier League chances and the Alonso revival could be the failure to find a better goalkeeper than the unreliable Robert Sanchez, who was at fault for both Fulham goals.

Tactically Alonso used a back three with Reece James operating in midfield but also dropping back into defence.

articles.title: 5 Teams Outside the CFB Top 25 Capable of a 2026 Playoff Run
articles.summary: The most straightforward way to explain expectations for college football teams is their placement in the preseason AP Top 25.
articles.body:
The most straightforward way to explain expectations for college football teams is their placement in the preseason AP Top 25.

If the consensus belief is a program will be a national contender, it'll be reflected in the rankings. If not, well, that's also clear to see. The hope for teams in the latter category is they'll prove the voters wrong.

Thanks to the College Football Playoff now featuring 12 teams, there is plenty of opportunity for that, too.

Look, history says we have a really good idea of the 2026 season's champion. Since the 2000 campaign, 21 of the 26 winners were preseason top-10 teams. Indiana was an outlier last year, yet the Hoosiers still opened at No. 20.

Orchestrating a run to the CFP, though, is a plausible ceiling for this group.

Opening the season at Oregon is a double-edged sword for Boise State.

Even without a win against the nation's No. 2 team—the expectation, to be sure—a competitive loss would be helpful in the perception department. On the other hand, a lopsided result may damage the Broncos.

But, hey, that's the nature of the sport. And there's certainly value in playing the hardest team on your schedule right away.

The remade Pac-12, while not easy, isn't exactly a gauntlet, either. Boise returns a veteran at quarterback with Maddux Madsen, while the backfield is stacked and defense is always reliable.

Early lessons could fuel a Playoff surge for the boys from the blue turf.

No team outside the AP Top 25 totaled more voting points than Clemson, which essentially landed at 26th in the initial poll. Nevertheless, the Tigers are set to kick off the season unranked.

Clemson's opener is at LSU, but that's not a decisive game. The more impactful moment for Dabo Swinney's team awaits in Week 5 when No. 7 Miami comes to town. If the Tigers capitalize on their home-field advantage and beat the 'Canes, Clemson's path to the ACC Championship Game is very apparent.

At that point, it does not matter if Clemson—which is turning the offense over to Christopher Vizzina in 2026—is among the nation's best teams. Win the ACC, and the Tigers are in the Playoff.

Swinney has taken a fair share of criticism lately, but he's still a two-time national champion. He'd have Clemson ready for the bright lights of the CFP.

Clemson ever-so-narrowly missed the preseason AP Top 25. Kansas State, meanwhile, did not receive a single vote.

Perhaps that's the correct view. After all, the Wildcats lost a bunch of production from a group that mustered a 6-6 record last year. Bullish as you might be on new coach Collin Klein—and place me in that camp—this is a rebuild.

Klein, the first coordinator of Avery Johnson's time at K-State, should be able to unlock a more consistent version of the dual-threat QB. Kansas State's schedule does not include Texas Tech, BYU or Utah, and a few other Big 12 notables—Houston, Oklahoma State and Arizona—each travel to Manhattan.

I am, metaphorically, not betting on Kansas State this season. Still, the dream of a CFP ascent is not too difficult to conceive.

When your roster is hovering around 80 new players compared to last season's squad, that is an unpredictable team.

Simultaneously, there's a nice infusion of talent at Oklahoma State. Eric Morris brought more than a dozen players from North Texas—including star players such as quarterback Drew Mestemaker, running back Caleb Hawkins and wide receiver Wyatt Young—and added many power-conference transfers.

The Cowboys are unpredictable, but not entirely unproven.

The schedule is much tougher than K-State's, for example, with the Pokes hosting Oregon and Texas Tech. OSU travels to Houston, Kansas State and Arizona State, as well. Simply attaining bowl eligibility, in hindsight, might be a win.

Before the year begins, however, this overhauled Oklahoma State roster is plenty intriguing as a CFP sleeper.

During both the 2024 and 2025 seasons, TCU posted an 8-4 record and closed the campaigns with a bowl victory. That's a quality two-year run on paper.

The problem, though, is the Horned Frogs never really cracked the national consciousness. They stumbled out to a 3-3 start in 2024 prior to a hot finish, then a midseason lull stung TCU last season.

It wouldn't be stunning to see this roster take the next jump forward.

Yes, much of that optimism is reliant on Harvard transfer Jaden Craig to boost the offense. However, the Horned Frogs have a good bit of experience, and the early-season schedule is favorable. They could announce themselves a real Big 12 threat with a home victory over BYU to open October, too.

TCU already wasn't far from contending. If the Horned Frogs are truly improved this season, they'll be capable of crashing the CFP.

articles.title: Aston Villa make contact with Crystal Palace for Jean-Philippe Mateta and approach AC Milan for Rafael Leao
articles.summary: Aston Villa interested in signing Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta and Rafael Leao from AC Milan; Mateta is a long-term target and Villa are serious about Leao; club looking to strengthen forward areas in Unai Emery's squad due to uncertainty about Ollie Watkins' future
articles.body:
Aston Villa have made initial contact with Crystal Palace for Jean-Philippe Mateta after also approaching AC Milan about signing winger Rafael Leao.

Villa are working on their potential forward options with Al Hilal pushing to sign striker Ollie Watkins.

Sky Sports News has reported that the Saudi Pro League side are in talks to sign Watkins and have had at least one bid rejected.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Aston Villa news & transfers🦁
  • Aston Villa fixtures & scores | FREE Villa highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Watkins was not included in the match-day squad for the 4-0 defeat to Brighton on Sunday and when asked for an explanation after the game, Villa boss Unai Emery told Sky Sports: "Ask him. I only can answer it by silence."

Reports have since emerged suggesting that the England striker returned to training on Monday and apologised to team-mates for his absence.

Mateta, who has one year left on his Palace deal, has been of interest to Villa since at least the winter transfer window.

The 29-year-old striker started for Palace in their 2-0 defeat to Everton at the weekend.

Reports have suggested there is a gap in valuation between Villa and Palace regarding Mateta.

Meanwhile, the club are serious about pursuing Leao, who has expressed an openness to the move.

Villa and Milan are in contact and will now negotiate in a bid to reach an agreement before Deadline Day on September 1.

Leao can play as a centre forward or on the left wing and scored nine goals and added three assists in 29 Serie A appearances last season.

Villa are also long-term admirers of Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, who is expected to leave before the deadline but also has interest from Napoli and several other clubs.

Sky Sports News previously reported Villa were expected to make a move to sign Jackson if Watkins was sold to Al Hilal.

Leao can replace Rogers' output and flexibility for Villa

Sky Sports' Patrick Rowe:

Aston Villa were forced to use Emi Buendia and Ross Barkley as makeshift forwards during their dismal 4-0 defeat to Brighton.

Ollie Watkins was missing from the squad due to uncertainty regarding his future, while both Tammy Abraham and 17-year-old Brian Madjo were sidelined with injury.

Unai Emery has watched on as his Europa League-winning squad was ripped apart across this summer. Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have gone. Watkins and Emiliano Martinez could follow suit.

The club desperately need reinforcements before Deadline Day on September 1. But Rafael Leao would not just be an ordinary body through the door.

The 27-year-old forward has long been linked with a move to the Premier League and in a bid to replace Rogers' output and flexibility across the forward line, Villa and Emery are turning their attention to him.

Capable of playing as the central forward, second striker or out on the left, Leao would mimic Rogers' presence in the squad with the same ability to drive at defences and threaten goal from all areas.

His stock in world football has dropped of late but look what Emery did for Marcus Rashford's career.

Villa can offer Champions League football, prominence in the starting line-up and the platform to impress in the Premier League. Leao offers Emery a crucial reinforcement and plugs the star-level gap left in the squad from player exits. A deal would work perfectly for both parties.

'Leao would be an incredible signing for Villa'

Former AC Milan and Chelsea goalkeeper Asmir Begovic speaking on Sky Sports:

"This wouldn't be good news, it'd be great news for Villa fans! Rafael Leao would be an incredible signing.

"I have played with him. I have seen the potential, pace, power and skill.

"He will be super suited to the Premier League. His game, the talent he has and the physical attributes he has will suit the Premier League.

"At Milan, he came through the ranks and really developed. He had good senior players and had consistency. Things started to change, a lot of managers started to change.

"It hasn't helped his consistency. Everyone has played him slightly differently. Look at Unai Emery and what he has done to some of the players at Aston Villa.

"Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins, taking their careers to the next level.

"Rafael Leao, working with Emery and getting the opportunity to be the main player at Villa, it would be huge."

articles.title: Aston Villa: The reality of the finances available to Unai Emery at Villa Park following a summer of upheaval
articles.summary: Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett assesses the situation at Aston Villa following a summer of upheaval and a dismal 4-0 defeat to Brighton to start the 2026/27 season; Villa feel confident Emery's future is secure but top clubs have an admiration for the Spaniard
articles.body:
All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.

Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

  • Problems mounting for threadbare Villa ahead of Arsenal
  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Aston Villa news & transfers🦁
  • Aston Villa fixtures & scores | FREE Villa highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football: Smash that easy button with these 5 destination offenses that have narrow usage trees
articles.summary: The teams that employ the shortest list of contributors are the most appealing for fantasy football.
articles.body:
One of the keys to a happy adult life is learning how to deal with traffic. Maybe you're navigating a trip to the airport, or trying to find the most seamless work commute. I prefer to shop on off-peak hours, and take a late lunch in a mostly-empty restaurant. Less gridlock, more happiness.

Keep that theme in mind as you're doing your fantasy football scouting for 2026. The NFL teams that employ the shortest list of regular contributors become destination offenses for fantasy managers. Keep it narrow , keep it simple.

We want you to smash that easy button as often as possible. Let's explore a few offenses that should be fun this year, as they look to be productive regularly but tied to a limited number of contributors. These are your narrow-usage offenses for 2026.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

So long as starting QB Joe Burrow stays healthy, this Cincinnati offense could go to the moon. And there won't be many seats taken on that spaceship, as almost the entire offense will be funneled through two star receivers (Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins ) and one do-it-all running back ( Chase Brown ). The Bengals have also had a horrible defense for three years running; even if it's mildly improved, pinball games are probably coming to Cincinnati. That makes the Bengals a potential carnival team as well, checking all the fun boxes.

They're not a perfect fit for this frame, as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum share backfield work (I prefer to draft Corum at cost) and the tight end room is super-crowded. But the Rams throw to their backs less than any other team, and veteran QB Matthew Stafford does very little with his legs. Puka Nacua had a robust 30.29% market share last year, and Davante Adams led the NFL in both red-zone targets and touchdown catches. The Rams don't have an impactful third WR looming on the depth chart, which means Nacua and Adams will once again be swimming in targets.

Detroit checks so many boxes when we're searching for a bankable offense. There's plenty of continuity here, a schedule heavy on indoor games and a bunch of beatable defenses coming to town. Jared Goff is a reliable veteran QB but not a runner, which is good for his teammates.

Fantasy Football: 3 big-name quarterbacks we're fading at ADP this season

Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026

Fantasy Football Running Back Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the RB profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook

Jahmyr Gibbs will have the backfield essentially to himself this year, slotting him as the consensus No. 1 pick. Amon-Ra St. Brown is a consistency king who fits in the middle of any first round. Jameson Williams took off last year when Sam LaPorta got hurt; this summer, we once again worry about a LaPorta injury. Even if the Big 4 all remain healthy, there's plenty to go around. Keep in mind second-year WR Isaac TeSlaa has been disappointing in camp, which tightens the overall concentration.

This one is a little tricky, as the Falcons haven't solved their QB problem yet. Tua Tagovailoa has been shaky this summer, and Michael Penix Jr. hasn't shown much through two seasons. But Atlanta didn't have great QB play last year, either, and Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. were all fantasy stars. Robinson and Pitts saved the best for last; Robinson was the best RB in the fantasy playoffs, and Pitts went nuclear in Week 15 (11-166-3), one of the best tight end games of all-time.

After Atlanta's Big 3 are selected, most rooms will ignore the rest of the Falcons. RB Brian Robinson Jr. is merely an insurance play (and sometimes a name-confusion click) and no support receiver here is commanding a top-200 pick. The Falcons will lean on their best players again this fall, and we like it that way.

The Dallas vibes are similar to the Cincinnati vibes, a star quarterback and productive offense trying to outscore the mediocre defense on the other side. The concentration isn't quite as tight in Dallas, as four primary players see regular work ( CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Javonte Williams , Jake Ferguson ), and Ryan Flournoy is an interesting third receiver. But Flournoy probably won't see a big role unless Lamb or Pickens get hurt, and QB Dak Prescott has cut back his running in the second half of his career. At the end of the day, we know where our Texas Toast is buttered.

articles.title: Liam Delap transfer: Nottingham Forest agree club-record deal to sign Chelsea striker
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea; striker moved to Stamford Bridge last summer, but scored just two goals in 41 games for the club; Chelsea could make a £20m profit having signed the 23-year-old for £30m
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea.

The transfer is understood to be worth at least £45m, which could reach £50m with add-ons.

The striker is scheduled to have a medical on Wednesday.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Forest news & transfers🔴⚪
  • Forest fixtures & scores | FREE Forest highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Delap had interest from a number of other Premier League clubs, including Everton, but Forest have secured his signing.

Chelsea signed Delap last summer for £30m from Ipswich and valued him at around £50m this summer.

They could be set for a £20m profit on a striker who scored two goals in 41 appearances last season.

Forest's previous record transfer saw Omari Hutchison join for £37.5m from Ipswich Town in August 2025.

Sherwood backs Forest's Delap move

Tim Sherwood speaking on Soccer Special:

"We know Liam's got the ability; he's shown that in the past. He needs to play on a regular basis now. He needs to stay fit.

"It never worked out at Chelsea. I never think he ever got a run in the team to give that striker the confidence; you need the manager to love you and play you every week, even if you're not playing well. I think he'll get that with Glasner - you've seen that with (Jean-Philippe Mateta) at Palace.

"He [Forest boss Oliver Glasner] likes to play with a big striker; he likes support. If he [Delap] can keep up with play, I think he'll score goals for Nottingham Forest, and I believe he will keep up with play.

"I think he's aggressive; he's got a lot of attributes to be a top, top striker, but Chelsea just did not work for him, and that's what happens.

"Forget about the price tag because the price tags all over the Premier League now are just ridiculous."

What other business could Forest do?

Forest are bringing in Delap to improve their striking options following Taiwo Awoniyi's £9m move to Coventry.

Oliver Glasner's side have been pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall as an Elliot Anderson replacement, but Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi insists he is staying in north London.

Forest could also add a right wing-back, with Dodo at Fiorentina a player of interest.

Dilane Bakwa is set to join Lille on loan, while centre-backs Zach Abbott and Tyler Bindon could also depart on temporary moves amid interest from Watford.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Gives Frustrated Reaction in Trending Video After Being Subbed Off at Halftime
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo did not seemed pleased during Monday's matchup against Al-Ettifaq, angrily coming off the pitch with Al-Nassr trailing by a 2-0 margin.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo did not seemed pleased during Monday's matchup against Al-Ettifaq, angrily coming off the pitch with Al-Nassr trailing by a 2-0 margin.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

The 41-year-old scored 28 goals and added two assists for Al-Nassr last season as the club won the Saudi Pro League title, its 11th league championship but first during the Ronaldo era. He's scored at least 25 league goals for Al-Nassr in the past three seasons.

The club won its first two games of the 2026-27 season but was off to a brutal start on Tuesday, as goalkeeper Bento was sent off in the 12th minute on a straight red and his replacement, Abdulrahman Al-Otaibi, allowed two howlers.

That put Al-Nassr in a 2-0 hole, though the club managed to salvage a 3-2 comeback victory behind a second-half brace from Sadio Mané and a goal from Abdulelah Al-Amri. João Félix finished with two assists.

Perhaps Ronaldo is in a better mood following the comeback effort.

articles.title: PFA Awards 2026: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win player of the year awards
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw win the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw have won the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.

Both were previously named the Football Writers' Association men's and women's footballers of the year for the 2025-26 season.

Fernandes, who last season broke the record for the most assists in a single Premier League campaign with 21, is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

It is a second win in three seasons for Shaw, who secured her third consecutive Women's Super League (WSL) golden boot with 21 goals as Man City were crowned champions.

City defender Nico O'Reilly succeeds Morgan Rogers as men's young player of the year, with the versatile 21-year-old cementing his place in the starting XI.

He contributed eight goal involvements (five goals) and nine clean sheets in 34 league outings, scoring twice, and was named player of the match as City beat Arsenal in the League Cup final.

Arsenal 's Olivia Smith retained her crown as the women's young player of the year, becoming only the second player after England international Lauren Hemp, to win the award on multiple occasions.

The Canada international, 22, scored 10 goals in all competitions after joining the Gunners for Â£1m last summer from Liverpool .

Individual success for record-breaker Fernandes

Although it was another trophy-less campaign for Man United, Fernandes enjoyed individual success, surpassing Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry's record of 20 assists in a Premier League campaign.

Fernandes set up his side's opener on the final day of the season against Brighton â and scored their third â to finish 2025-26 with nine goals and 21 assists in 35 league outings. Man City's Rayan Cherki was the second-most prolific provider, with 12 assists.

His haul helped United finish third and secure Champions League football.

In total, the 31-year-old scored nine goals and contributed 22 assists in 37 matches in all competitions.

Fernandes, who joined the club from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020, beat Arsenal trio Gabriel Magalhaes, David Raya, and Declan Rice and Man City attackers Cherki and Erling Haaland to the award.

He is only the second Portuguese to be named player of the year, following back-to-back wins for former Man United winger Cristiano Ronaldo in 2007 and 2008.

Shaw scored 21 goals in 22 appearances as Man City clinched their second WSL title.

The Jamaica international registered hat-tricks against Aston Villa (four goals) and Tottenham and scored twice against West Ham on the final day of the season to become the first player to score 20 or more goals in three different WSL seasons.

Shaw is the first player to win three WSL golden boots, moving clear of two-time winners Vivienne Miedema and Sam Kerr.

The 29-year-old scored a further five goals, including the opener in the final, as Man City won the FA Cup.

Shaw, the third individual to win multiple PFA women's player of the year awards, joining Lucy Bronze and Fran Kirby, previously completed the PFA and FWA double following the 2023-24 campaign.

Team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Aston Villa 's Kirsty Hanson, Chelsea 's Lauren James, Man United's Jess Park, and Arsenal 's Alessia Russo were also shortlisted.

Arsenal and Man City dominate team of the year

The Premier League team of the year, as voted for by the players, was dominated by champions Arsenal and runners-up Man City.

Arsenal only conceded 27 goals last season, with that impressive record reflected in the selections of goalkeeper Raya and defenders Gabriel, William Saliba and Jurrien Timber named alongside midfielder Rice.

Man City have four representatives â O'Reilly, Cherki, Haaland and Antoine Semenyo â with Man United's Fernandes and team of the year debutant Igor Thiago ( Brentford ) completing the XI.

The WSL side features three players apiece from champions Man City, Chelsea , and Arsenal , with Man United's Park and Tottenham defender Toko Koga the only players selected from outside the top three sides.

Premier League team of the year: David Raya ( Arsenal ); Jurrien Timber ( Arsenal ), William Saliba ( Arsenal ), Gabriel Magalhaes ( Arsenal ), Nico O'Reilly (Man City); Bruno Fernandes (Man United), Declan Rice ( Arsenal ), Rayan Cherki (Man City); Erling Haaland (Man City), Antoine Semenyo (Man City), Igor Thiago ( Brentford ).

WSL team of the year: Hannah Hampton ( Chelsea ); Kerstin Casparij (Man City), Toko Koga ( Tottenham ), Ellie Carpenter ( Chelsea ), Emily Fox ( Arsenal ); Yui Hasegawa (Man City), Mariona Caldentey ( Arsenal ), Jess Park (Man United); Bunny Shaw (Man City), Alessia Russo ( Arsenal ), Lauren James ( Chelsea ).

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd captain wins 2025/26 PFA Players' Player of the Year as Bunny Shaw wins women's award
articles.summary: Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year as Man City’s Bunny Shaw wins women’s award for second time; men's Young Player of the Year handed to Man City's Nico O'Reilly as Arsenal's Olivia Smith picks up women's prize; Sir Kenny Dalglish receives merit award
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned the men's PFA Players' Player of the Year for the 2025/26 season, as Manchester City's Bunny Shaw won the women's award for a second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcame a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE!
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009/10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again, having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

O'Reilly and Smith scoop young player awards

Arsenal's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford striker Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by team-mates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo.

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in the team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

EFL awards revealed as Dalglish picks up merit prize

In the EFL, former Middlesbrough midfielder Hayden Hackey, who joined Premier League side Everton this summer in a £24m deal, won the Championship PFA Players' Player of the Year.

Dom Ballard, who joined Bristol City from Leyton Orient earlier this summer, claimed the award in League One, while Swindon striker Aaron Drinan picked up the League Two prize.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland's most capped player, having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June that he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

articles.title: How Celtic's Champions League capitulation unfolded
articles.summary: BBC Scotland guides you through the timeline in Celtic's Champions League reverse in Austria.
articles.body:
All applicable, all too familiar, all can be levied at Celtic after their Champions League qualification blunder away to LASK .

A night that started full of hope and optimism as Celtic edged four goals clear on aggregate after 21 minutes ended in deep humiliation in a 5-4 aggregate defeat after extra time.

At the same stage last season, their disastrous loss to Kairat Almaty ultimately cast a long shadow over their season and was the nexus point for an overflow of negative fan sentiment towards the club.

Here's how Celtic's nightmare evening unfolded.

23' LASK 0-1 Celtic (agg 0-4) - McGregor

LASK started strongly but nowhere near as well as they finished it.

A few chances passed them by before Yang Hyun-jun showed great poise wide on the left to drive forward, cut inside, and pull it back for captain Callum McGregor to step on to.

His strike was deflected past a helpless goalkeeper and gave his side a 4-0 aggregate lead after 21 minutes.

"We're having a party in the Champions League" was the chant coming from the pocket of Celtic fans over on the far side.

Their passage to the Champions League seemed nigh on inevitable.

Samuel Adeniran nodded off target just after the restart and then pulled one wide - the warning signs were there.

LASK had passed up a glut of chances but didn't need to work hard to draw level on the night.

Moses Usor pounced on Benjamin Nygren's pass straight into his path and coolly finished to spark a little bit of hope inside the Raiffeisen Arena.

Surely Celtic had banished their Kairat demons? Surely this would be scant consolation for the hosts?

"It's a lovely composed finish, but that is an absolute gift," James McFadden said on BBC Radio Scotland.

An uneventful opening few minutes to the second half came and went without note.

Then Robert Ljubicic gave the home fans an almighty dose of confidence.

Defender Auston Trusty was caught lacking, and Ljubicic was afforded far too much time to shape and shoot on the edge of the area.

Viljami Sinisalo was beaten low to his left, and Celtic were utterly stunned.

"That is unacceptable," McFadden said on BBC Radio Scotland when describing Trusty's defending.

Major cracks were exposed in Celtic's ability to deal with LASK's rampant press and front-foot football.

LASK took the lead on the night. 48 minutes, 2-1.

LASK pulled further into the lead on the night and were only one goal back on aggregate thanks to a sensational Adeniran strike.

Alarm bells were blaring for the visitors.

Sascha Horvath did ever so well to advance the ball, lift his head, and roll it into his team-mate's path, who stepped on to the ball and curled it in from 25 yards with a sumptuous first-time effort.

Celtic had no response. The hosts were the only side looking likely to score.

The team were flat-footed and bereft of all confidence; from this point on, the game was played almost exclusively in their half.

For all of LASK's huffing and puffing, they were unable to find the all-important leveller in the tie.

The bar was struck, crosses whizzed across the goal, and chance after chance was spurned.

The home side chucked everything they had at Celtic. Corners were whipped in, headers glanced wide, and through balls drilled into the area.

They couldn't get it over the line, though. That one final bounce of the ball didn't drop in their favour.

Sinisalo pulled off a terrific stop to slap Alemao's close-range header away, but no-one had picked up Florian Flecker, who nodded in the equaliser as the time ticked into the four added minutes shown by the fourth official.

McFadden said: "Credit LASK because they haven't given in, but Celtic have created problems for themselves."

Celtic had come so close to the Champions League proper, they were now clinging on.

Often, extra time is a damp squib these days, particularly in big games.

Neither side wants to lose, and both will be happy to take a chance on penalties.

With 11 minutes still to play, Luke McCowan won the ball back for his side, but he was far too pedestrian in his decision-making, and he was dispossessed.

Another Adeniran goal from outside the box punished Celtic yet again.

The Champions League now felt like a distant dream, in stark contrast to the tangible next step of earlier on.

Sinisalo got down to make a huge save to deny Adeniran a hat-trick from the spot, but a few minutes later it meant nothing.

120 minutes. 5-4 on aggregate. Celtic's humiliation complete.

"It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted," former Celtic manager Neil Lennon told Amazon Prime. "Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"Huge credit to LASK. They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

articles.title: LASK v Celtic: Martin O'Neill takes responsibility
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
articles.body:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded Published 1 hour ago

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria.

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: " It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."

Mariona Caldentey , last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo .

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in a team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton , Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James .

Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland 's most capped player having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.
paragraphs: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City 's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time.
Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne .
The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.
Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.
He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."
The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.
Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognized by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.
The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

Arsenal 's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.
Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.
The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland , Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo .

articles.title: Football safety remains focus as new CTE study released
articles.summary: As football season kicks off for Durham Public Schools, athletic leaders are taking steps to keep student-athletes safer.
articles.body:
As football season gets underway for Durham Public Schools, safety remains a top concern as researchers continue to learn more about chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE.

CTE is a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts.

"It's a progressive neurodegenerative condition that comes from sustaining repeated blows to the head over time," neurologist Leah Croll said.

A new study found that at least 25% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE. Croll said head impacts do not have to result in a concussion to increase the risk of developing the disease.

"They can be what we call sub-concussive hits," Croll said. "Over time, having more and more instances where you're hit in the head, that can contribute to increasing your risk for developing this condition."

Advocates described the study as a "sobering reminder that football carries real risks."

In a statement to ABC11, the NFL said the league "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts."

CTE can only be diagnosed after death, meaning research has relied heavily on brains donated by players and their families. Researchers say that limitation makes it difficult to fully understand how the disease develops and how it can be prevented or treated in living people.

"It really slows down our research efforts when it comes to prevention and treatment of CTE, and that's a huge problem, particularly when it comes to kids," Croll said.

The study comes as a 17-year-old high school quarterback in Wisconsin died after suffering an on-field injury during a game.

"Any time a student-athlete loses their life or suffers a severe head trauma is concerning to everyone," Durham Public Schools athletic director David Hackney said. "We try to take every safety measure to try to prevent those things from happening."

Durham Public Schools uses Guardian Caps, soft-shell padding worn over traditional football helmets. Hackney said the equipment has helped student-athletes.

"I think Guardian Caps is a big step, but we can take it a step further," Hackney said.

Hackney said licensed professionals are also on-site at Durham football games to evaluate injuries. After an injury, an athletic trainer assesses when it is safe for a student-athlete to return to action.

"We monitor concussion protocols," Hackney said. "Our athletic trainers do an awesome job of making sure they're following up with the student-athlete, as well as their parents, to make sure that they're following all those safety measures and that they take every precaution before they are allowed back on the field."

School officials said those measures are intended to reduce risks and help protect student-athletes throughout the football season.
